strategy_name: The Squeeze Play: volatility-cycle breakout from compression
mechanism: volatility runs in cycles - high-volatility trends are followed by low-volatility consolidation; once compression is confirmed, the next expansion is imminent, and traders caught on the wrong side of the breakout fuel it (longer consolidation -> stronger breakout)
setup_summary: Daily chart: price consolidates into a narrowing range; 20-period EMA flattens; ATR(14) is falling; Bollinger band width is near its lows. Draw trend lines forming a symmetrical triangle; go long on a break above the upper trendline or short below the lower trendline. Exits are mapped IN ADVANCE in both directions (prior support/resistance, Fibonacci retracements of the prior move, round numbers).
trigger_invalidation: Setup only valid if all three contraction confirmations agree (flat 20-EMA, falling ATR, falling band width); if volatility is not compressing, no trade. A false break: stop placed on the far side of the trendline; thesis invalid if price closes back inside the triangle.
risk_geometry: Entry on trendline break (either direction); stop on the far side of the trendline; exits pre-mapped at prior S/R, Fibonacci, round numbers; partial exit at first target with stop moved to breakeven.
quote: The longer the amount of time spent in the consolidation phase, the stronger the breakout tends to be... there are likely to be a large number of traders who are caught on the 'wrong side' of the market... As these traders cover their positions, they provide fuel for the breakout.
chapter_anchor: Chapter 13 'The Squeeze Play', pp.169-180
notes: Volatility compression-expansion is pronounced in BTC perps (funding + leverage amplify the trapped-position fuel). Fully specifiable: ATR/Bollinger-width contraction thresholds, triangle-break entry, pre-mapped exits - fits V8's frozen-ref discipline. The 'longer consolidation = stronger breakout' claim is a falsifiable hypothesis to test on BTCUSDT 1h/4h. Register as new expert_family proposal (data-ready, no block).

strategy_name: Flag and pennant continuation with flagpole-measured geometry
mechanism: a sharp directional thrust (flagpole) expresses committed aggressive buying/selling; the small counter-slope consolidation (flag) or converging consolidation (pennant) is weak hands unloading; the aggressor side resumes and the pattern resolves as a continuation breakout in the pole's direction
setup_summary: Intraday chart: a sharp 100-200 pip thrust (flagpole) is followed by a small consolidation (pennant = two lines converging like a symmetrical triangle; flag = two parallel lines sloping against the pole). Entry order = 10% of flagpole height above the pole top (long) / below the pole bottom (short); stop = 25% of pole height below/above the ENTRY (not the pole top); first exit = 1R (partial, stop to breakeven); second exit = pole height measured from the pole top.
trigger_invalidation: No entry if price clears the flag's line but fails to reach 10%-above-pole-top (filtered example: the flag breakout that cannot clear the pole top is an inferior entry that fails); if the initial move is not sharp/sudden, the pattern's reliability is void.
risk_geometry: Entry: resting order at pole_top + 0.10*pole_height; stop: entry - 0.25*pole_height; exit1 = +1R with stop to breakeven; exit2 = pole_top + pole_height. Geometry is pole-scaled (fixed-percent, volatility-adaptive).
quote: Our entry will be at a point above the flagpole, by an amount equal to 10 percent of the flagpole... the stop will be placed a number of pips equal to 25 percent of the height of the flagpole.
chapter_anchor: Chapter 12 'Flags and Pennants', pp.153-168
notes: Fully mechanical and falsifiable (impulse + consolidation geometry prices entry/stop/targets), corroborated by the classic Edwards-Magee continuation-pattern literature. The 10%/25% pole-relative parameters are tuned to FX intraday scales and untested on BTC 1h; main cost is the pattern-detection feature (pole + consolidation shape) in marketstate. Backlog candidate; impulse-pullback-continuation is common in crypto.

strategy_name: The Interest Rate Edge: carry the interest-rate differential with a forward-looking exit
mechanism: in every pair trade one is long one currency and short the other; being long the higher-yielding currency collects the interest-rate differential daily, and leverage magnifies the yield on capital; carry entrants' buying pressure can accelerate the trend, and markets are forward-looking so the trade unwinds when policy signals say the differential will stop widening
setup_summary: Long the higher-yielding currency versus the lower-yielding one (e.g., long USD/JPY when the Fed is hiking and BoJ is at ~0%) when the differential is positive and expected to widen. Hold for months collecting the differential daily; exit on central-bank forward guidance that the differential will stop widening - the USD/JPY 2005 example dissolved into a range while the differential was still at its 4.25% peak because markets priced the expected peak.
trigger_invalidation: Exit when policy signals (central-bank statements/forward guidance) indicate the differential will narrow, even if the differential itself is still large - 'financial markets are forward looking'.
risk_geometry: No fixed stop; hold for months; risk is differential narrowing and adverse exchange-rate moves; leverage (50:1 to 200:1 in the book) is the risk multiplier - carry is the 'double-edged sword'.
quote: The trader who is long the higher yielding of the two currencies collects interest on the trade... This creates a 'chicken-and-egg' scenario; is the pair rising because traders are entering to collect the interest, or is the relative strength and weakness of the two economies causing the pair to rally?
chapter_anchor: Chapter 15 'The Interest Rate Edge', pp.193-200
notes: The perp analogue is funding: the perp-vs-spot funding rate is the carry yield and funding expectations are forward-looking (corroborates the starter ids funding_carry / carry_unwind). But a single BTCUSDT 1h expert cannot 'go long the high-yielder, short the low-yielder' - the idea becomes a cross-sectional funding/short-basis signal (cross_market feature), not a standalone directional expert. Also relevant to the simulator cost model: funding accrual must be modeled for hold-forever style experts.

strategy_name: Three-regime doctrine: proper-order MAs + ADX for trend/range classification
mechanism: markets are in one of three states (trending, range-bound, consolidating) and each requires different techniques; MA proper order and ADX classify the state; traders who 'fall in love' with a technique that worked in one regime lose when the regime changes
setup_summary: Classify regime per instrument: UPTREND if 10>20>50>200 SMA/EMA order holds, DOWNTREND if 200>50>20>10, RANGE if the MAs are jumbled/flat ('spaghetti'), CONSOLIDATION if price is trapped in a narrowing area. ADX >35 and rising = strongly trending. Use trend techniques only in trending regimes, range techniques only in ranges, and switch when the regime changes.
trigger_invalidation: Re-evaluate regime continuously; the 2004 USD/CHF example shows a trend regime decaying into consolidation while traders who kept trading trend technique got hurt; a false tendency (e.g., 'euro strong on Thursday') is a coincidence, not a tendency, and has coin-flip odds minus the spread.
risk_geometry: No entry geometry - this is a gating filter that decides WHICH expert family may fire.
quote: The 10-period simple moving average (SMA) is located above the 20-period SMA, which is above the 50-period SMA, which is above the 200-period SMA: 10 > 20 > 50 > 200... the ADX indicator's giving a reading above 35 and rising would be an indication of a strongly trending market.
chapter_anchor: Chapter 4 'Trends' pp.39-42; Chapter 6 'Understanding Trends and Tendencies', pp.53-62
notes: This is the book's central methodology thesis and maps directly onto V8's need to gate trend vs range experts (rule 14 complexity discipline and regime-dependent expert activation). Propose trend/regime features in marketstate: proper-order MA alignment flag, ADX(14)>35 rising, and a jumbled-MA range flag; use as a hard gate (e.g., trend_pullback only fires in trending regime). Also the 'don't fall in love with a technique' lesson is a lifecycle/portfolio-level methodology note.

strategy_name: Session-volume breakout filter: trade high-volume breakouts, fade low-volume ones
mechanism: high-volume moves are real because significant capital is committed; in low-volume windows, orders that normally could not move the market now can, and institutions may push price to execute order pools for commission - so low-volume breakouts are suspect and fadeable
setup_summary: For intraday breakouts of triangles and S/R levels: breakouts during high-volume sessions (London open / London-New York overlap) are treated as legitimate; breakouts during low-volume windows (late Asian session, late US session) are suspect and should not be traded in the breakout direction - they may be faded instead. The EUR/USD 1.2000 example: the false break came late in the Asian session (June 24), the real break at ~14:30 GMT during the London/NY overlap (July 1). Combine with the ascending/descending-triangle directional bias and the prior-trend filter (breakout in the direction of the prior trend is more compelling).
trigger_invalidation: A breakout in a low-volume window is invalidated as a breakout signal (fade instead); after ~14:00-15:00 NY or when volume dissipates, breakout signals are unreliable.
risk_geometry: Entry on triangle-break; use prior-trend filter and volume/session filter as gates; stop beyond the broken level.
quote: a breakout is considered to be significant if it occurs on high volume, and is considered less reliable if it occurs on low volume... if a breakout does occur during a low-volume time of day, it would be acceptable to 'fade' – or trade against – the breakout.
chapter_anchor: Chapter 11 'Keys to Intraday Breakouts', pp.145-152
notes: Crypto perps have no session bell, but they do have a participation/volatility clock: the UTC 0:00 funding boundary, Asian/European/US overlap hours, and weekend low-participation windows. Propose a participation feature (rolling volume/volatility percentile or a session-clock label) used to gate breakout experts (volatility_breakout, NEW_flag_pennant, failed_breakout) - trade breakouts when participation is high, treat low-participation breakouts as suspect. This is the transferable kernel of both Chapter 11 and the rejected Boomerang.

strategy_name: Throwback/Pullback Completion Reentry (Breakout Retest)
setup_summary: After an upward (downward) breakout from any chart pattern, price returns to the breakout price or pattern boundary within 30 days (throwback/pullback). Enter long once the throwback completes: (A) close back above the pattern top, or (B) a higher peak and higher valley, or (C) close above the highest peak between the breakout and the throwback low. Throwbacks occur ~58% of the time (10,305 patterns; 60% for ascending triangles); in 65% of cases price resumes the breakout direction and rises, and in 25% of ascending-triangle throwbacks price drops below the pattern bottom.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: breakout close beyond the pattern boundary, then a loop back to the breakout level within 30 bars, then a completion signal (close back through the pattern top / higher peak+valley / close above the highest peak between breakout and throwback low). Invalidation: throwback dips too deep and closes below the pattern bottom (thesis fails — stop out; this is the main risk of the setup), or no throwback ever forms (missed move).
risk_geometry: Entry: next-bar open after throwback-completion signal (Option C usually gives the best results in the book's scan). Stop: penny below the throwback low or pattern bottom. Target: measure-rule projection; note patterns WITH throwbacks underperform those without (ascending triangles avg 28% vs 42%; head-and-shoulders bottoms 33% vs 42%). Expiry: throwback must complete within 30 days.
quote: A throwback occurs after an upward breakout when price returns to the breakout price or chart pattern boundary within 30 days.
chapter_anchor: Ch. 6 (Throwbacks and Pullbacks); Ch. 20 (The Throwback Buy Setup)
notes: Refines V8's DATA_BLOCKED breakout_retest backlog family by supplying the entry trigger (throwback completion) and the deep-throwback invalidation. 30-day window → 30 bars on 1h. Deep-throwback risk is amplified by crypto leverage; stop discipline is the edge here.

strategy_name: Busted Pattern Reversal (failed breakout that reverses and trends)
setup_summary: A confirmed chart pattern breaks out in one direction, price moves LESS than 10% before reversing, and then closes beyond the OPPOSITE boundary of the pattern (a 'bust'); enter at the open the day after that bust close. Single-busted patterns perform as well or better than non-busted: busted descending triangles rise >=10% above the pattern top 70% of the time (avg +29%), rectangles that single-bust average +61% vs +33% non-busted, and ascending triangles bust 40% of the time (single busts avg +40%).
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: (1) breakout close in one direction, (2) move <10% before reversing, (3) close through the opposite boundary of the pattern. Invalidation: double/triple bust — price re-crosses and closes beyond the ORIGINAL breakout side again (triangles double/triple-bust ~6-7%, symmetrical triangles double-bust most at 7%); repeated whipsaw means the pattern never establishes a direction. Sell side (Ch. 25): if an upward breakout busts downward, treat as a strong sell signal (28% hold win rate).
risk_geometry: Entry: buy/sell at the open the day after the bust close. Stop: for busted H&S tops the book places a stop below the lowest valley in the pattern; generally the pattern's far boundary. Target: measure rule projected from the busted direction (26-40% avg on single busts). Expiry: none stated; expect double-bust risk.
quote: A busted ascending triangle occurs when price breaks out in one direction, moves less than 10 percent before reversing, and continues in the new direction to close above the top or below the bottom of the triangle.
chapter_anchor: Ch. 22 (Busted Pattern Buy Setups); Ch. 25 (Busted Pattern Sell Signals)
notes: V8's failed_breakout expert (liquidity_vacuum_reentry, SHORT) is one instantiation of this — a busted top. This book generalizes the bust to both directions and any pattern shape, and supplies the <10% threshold, single/double/triple-bust counting, and per-pattern bust rates (bump patterns bust less than trendline patterns).
book: Visual Guide to Chart Patterns 2012

strategy_name: Partial Decline Predicts Upward Breakout (rectangle)
setup_summary: Within a valid rectangle (at least 2-3 touches of each trendline), price touches the top trendline and then pulls back but stops WELL ABOVE the bottom trendline before reversing upward — the 'partial decline' — predicting an immediate upward breakout 89% of the time (two studies: 69 rectangle bottoms, 170 rectangle tops).
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: valid rectangle in place + a dip after a top-trendline touch that fails to approach the bottom trendline, then an upward reversal. Invalidation: the dip reaches deep into the rectangle (near/through the bottom trendline) — not a partial decline; or no upward breakout follows within a handful of bars — thesis void.
risk_geometry: Entry: buy stop a penny above the top trendline, filled on the breakout. Stop: penny below the rectangle bottom (or below the partial-decline low). Target: rectangle-height measure rule. Expiry: immediate — the setup predicts an imminent breakout, so a delayed breakout weakens the signal.
quote: A partial decline correctly predicts an immediate upward breakout 89 percent of the time according to two studies I did using 69 rectangle bottoms and another with 170 rectangle tops.
chapter_anchor: Ch. 18 (Basic Buy Setups — Rectangle Buy Signal)
notes: Small samples (69+170) but an unusually specific and falsifiable pre-breakout signal; range structures are common on 1h BTC. The top-touch-then-shallow-dip geometry is a distinct behavior from V8's existing sweep/pullback experts.

strategy_name: Pattern Proximity to Trend Start (performance filter)
setup_summary: Chart patterns that form within ~3 months of a trend start outperform patterns late in a long trend. Ascending triangles within 3 months of trend start avg +39% vs +29% for longer; double bottoms with short-term (<3mo) inbound trend avg +42% vs +30% for long-term trends; H&S bottoms 40%/36%/33% by trend length. Define trend start as the extreme beyond which price moved at least 20%.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: locate the trend start (the high/low beyond which price changed >=20%); if pattern-to-start distance <3 months, prefer the setup. Invalidation: a pattern appearing well into a long trend may signal the END of the trend regardless of breakout direction (Ch. 17) — treat late-trend patterns as exhaustion warnings, not entries.
risk_geometry: No direct entry/stop/target; a regime/selection filter applied before entry. The 20% trend-start definition is concrete and computable.
quote: The longer the price trend leading to the start of a chart pattern, the worse the performance.
chapter_anchor: Ch. 19 (Failures); Ch. 23 (Trading Setups and Tips — Trend Start, Double Bottoms)
notes: Maps naturally to V8 trend/time feature groups and to the regime filter: candidate episodes can be gated on distance-from-trend-start, and late-trend patterns can feed a trend-exhaustion warning.

strategy_name: Trendline Break as Trend-Change/Exit Signal
setup_summary: In an uptrend draw an external trendline along the minor lows (hugging bar ends, not slicing price); a close below the line is a sell/exit signal — a hint of trend change, not a guarantee. Shallow trendlines (45 degrees or less) have staying power while steep ones flame out quickly; widely spaced touches make a line more significant; rising volume into the break powers a larger decline. Lower highs and lower lows after the break confirm the change.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: close below the up-sloping trendline (or close above a down-sloping line for shorts) — exit at the next bar open. Invalidation: a single close is only a hint; price can pierce and recover, so the line-drawing convention (internal vs external) controls whipsaw rate — require the close plus structure confirmation (lower highs/lower lows).
risk_geometry: Exit at next-bar open after the close below the line; no stop/target — used as a dead-thesis/exit rule. Book tip: switch to a longer timeframe when trading trendlines to ignore noise.
quote: In a rising price trend, draw trendlines along the valleys to detect a change in trend, from up to down. Steep trendlines stop trending sooner than shallow ones.
chapter_anchor: Ch. 3 (Trendlines — Guidelines); Ch. 27 (Trendline Sell Signals)
notes: Trendlines are scale-invariant; on 1h BTC a close-below-uptrendline rule is a clean lifecycle/dead-thesis exit complementing V8's still_valid refs. The book asserts 'I proved this' for wide-spaced touches and shallow>steep but publishes no numbers here.

strategy_name: Dual Momentum / Global Equities Momentum (GEM)
mechanism: Relative-strength momentum selects the strongest asset; a 12-month absolute-momentum gate on the selected asset decides risk-on vs. de-risked safe harbor, so trend persistence is harvested only when the trend itself is positive.
setup_summary: Monthly: compute trailing 12-month total return for each candidate risky asset (e.g., S&P 500 vs ACWI ex-US); pick the higher one; if its 12-month return beats the risk-free reference (T-bill), hold it for the next month; otherwise hold the safe harbor (aggregate bonds). Reported 1974-2013: GEM avg annual 17.43%, SD 12.64%, Sharpe 0.87, max drawdown 22.7%, ~1.35 switches/yr, significant alpha under Fama-French-Carhart factor models.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: selected asset's 12-month return > risk-free reference at month-end. Invalidation: selected asset's 12-month return < risk-free reference, or relative ranking flips -> rotate or move to safe harbor next bar.
risk_geometry: Entry at monthly close signal (NEXT_BAR_CLOSE analog), no per-position stop; exit is the trend gate (absolute momentum negative) not a price stop; holding period = one month with rebalance; safe-harbor asset replaces the risky asset, so this is a two-asset-state machine, not an R-multiple stop/target.
quote: We first compare the S&P 500 to the ACWI ex-U.S. over the past year and select whichever one has performed better. We then check to see if our selected index has done better than U.S. Treasury bills. If it has, we invest in that index. If it has not, we invest instead in U.S. aggregate bonds.
chapter_anchor: Ch. 8, Global Equities Momentum (Applied Dual Momentum)
notes: Strongest strategy in the book: 40y of data, decade-by-decade consistency, factor-model alpha, 12-month lookback cross-validated across both momentum forms. In crypto-perp terms the rotation universe is BTC/ETH/major alts and the safe harbor is flat (USDT) or a stablecoin delta rather than T-bills; the T-bill reference maps to funding/zero-carry. Requires the cross_market feature group (MarketState per instrument) and a long cadence that conflicts with V8's 1h bar horizon - registry decision before code; lands in src/v8/experts/ + docs/EXPERTS_REGISTRY.yaml.

strategy_name: Absolute (time-series) momentum trend filter / overlay
mechanism: An asset's own trailing return is positively autocorrelated: sign of trailing 12-month excess return predicts continuation, so the trend filter both gates entries and provides a re-entry-capable replacement for a stop.
setup_summary: On any asset: if trailing 12-month excess return (asset return minus risk-free reference) > 0, hold long; if < 0, exit to the safe harbor (T-bills/bonds) until it turns positive again; re-evaluate monthly. 12-month lookback is the best formation (highest Sharpe, best across decades 1974-2012) and beats all 2-18 month alternatives; applied to S&P 500 it cut max drawdown from >50% to <30% and raised annual return ~200bp vs buy-and-hold.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: trailing 12-month excess return > 0 at evaluation. Invalidation: trailing 12-month excess return < 0 -> de-risk to safe harbor; re-entry is automatic when the sign flips back (unlike a stop, which has no re-entry).
risk_geometry: Monthly evaluation; exit is the trend-sign change, not a price stop; it acts as a dormant stop-loss during bull phases with inherent re-entry; no R-multiple target; will not catch sharp corrections (Oct 1987) but avoids prolonged bear markets.
quote: our strategy simply defines absolute momentum as being positive when the excess return (asset return less the Treasury bill return) over the formation (look-back) period is positive. We hold a long position in our selected assets during these times.
chapter_anchor: Appendix B (Absolute Momentum) and Ch. 7 (Understanding Absolute Momentum)
notes: This is the single most falsifiable, universally corroborated mechanism in the book (Moskowitz-Ooi-Pedersen; Hurst et al. back to 1903, Sharpe>1). For V8: add a trailing-window return-sign feature to the trend feature group and consider a lifecycle rule that de-risks when the regime trend turns negative - the book explicitly argues this is superior to a hard stop because it auto-re-enters. Also a REFINE candidate for existing trend_pullback/failed_breakout still_valid logic.

strategy_name: Proximity to 52-week high momentum
mechanism: Nearness to the 52-week high is an anchor for recently-arrived good news; being close to the high dominates trailing return as a predictor of continuation.
setup_summary: Rank assets by ratio of current price to trailing 52-week high; buy those near the high that also have high 6-month past returns. George & Hwang (US stocks 1963-2001): profits from nearness-to-high plus top 6-month returns beat profits from 6-month returns alone; nearness to the 52-week high dominated the forecasting power of past returns.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: price within some threshold of the trailing 52-week high with positive 6-month return. Invalidation: price falls materially below the reference high or the anchor rolls lower; thesis weakens as the 52-week high reference falls.
risk_geometry: Entry on strength near the reference high; no stop/target stated in the book - it is a cross-sectional ranking signal; the frozen reference (windowed high) mirrors V8's frozen_ref pattern in failed_breakout but with opposite polarity.
quote: profits based on nearness to the 52-week high plus the highest returns over the past six months were superior to profits based solely on the highest returns over the past six months. Nearness to the 52-week high dominated the forecasting power of past returns.
chapter_anchor: Ch. 9, Mo' Better Momentum (Proximity to 52-Week Highs)
notes: Corroborated within this book by Darvas, Dreyfus and O'Neil ('buy stocks making new highs') and by Donchian channel-breakout lineage. Well suited to crypto perps (24/7, frequent new highs, no exchange gaps so the reference is clean); on 1h bars the 52-week window is ~8760 bars, so this is a long-horizon location feature. Candidate new expert family near_high_continuation in src/v8/experts/; register first given complexity budget.

strategy_name: Fresh vs stale momentum winners
mechanism: Recency/attention: winners whose strength is fresh (recent 12m up, prior 12m weak) outperform stale winners (up in both windows) because fresh strength attracts flow and is less crowded.
setup_summary: Double-sort by relative price strength in months 1-12 (skip most recent month) and months 13-24. Fresh winners (strong in 1-12, weak in 13-24) outperformed stale winners (strong in both) by 0.43% per month on US stocks 1926-2006 (Chen, Kadan, Kose 2009).
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: asset ranked in top quintile of trailing 12m momentum but was relatively weak in the prior 12m. Invalidation: the asset becomes a stale winner (strong in both windows) or its 12m rank decays out of the top quintile.
risk_geometry: Cross-sectional ranking signal, no per-trade stop/target in the book; usable as a quality filter on any momentum/trend entry rather than a standalone entry.
quote: fresh winners outperformed stale winners by 0.43% per month.
chapter_anchor: Ch. 9, Mo' Better Momentum (Fresh Momentum)
notes: V8-native use: a recency filter for the trend_following family - e.g., a regime where a fresh pump (recent up, prior flat/down) is a stronger continuation candidate than an extended uptrend. For single-instrument BTCUSDT 1h the prior 12m/second window maps to two long lookbacks (e.g., 365/730 daily bars); most natural as a trend-quality feature or variant of the dual-momentum family.

strategy_name: Accelerating momentum / convex price trajectory
mechanism: Investor attention amplifies momentum when the price path is convex (accelerating) rather than concave (decelerating), so trend quality depends on trajectory curvature, not just cumulative return.
setup_summary: Regress daily returns on time-squared over the formation window; positive coefficient = convex (accelerating) trajectory. Among positive-momentum stocks, convex winners had significantly higher forward returns and 3-factor alphas than concave winners (Chen & Yu, US 1962-2011); Docherty & Hurst (trend salience, Australia 1992-2012) corroborate with a double-sort on short-term slope vs 12-month average return.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: momentum positive AND trajectory curvature convex (or short-term slope > 12-month average rate). Invalidation: curvature turns concave/decelerating while momentum is still positive - thesis for the acceleration component dies even if raw momentum persists.
risk_geometry: Ranking/quality signal; no stop or target in the book. Usable as an entry-quality gate on trend entries; in V8 could be a volatility/trajectory feature over the lookback.
quote: The authors showed that ignoring positive momentum stocks with concave price trajectories is the key to earning higher momentum returns.
chapter_anchor: Ch. 9, Mo' Better Momentum (Accelerating Momentum)
notes: Plausible refinement for the trend family (parabolic vs grinding phases matter in crypto perps), but only two supporting studies and no clear parameterization in the book - keep as a backlog_family candidate pending frozen-OOS evidence. Note book also flags Paul Tudor Jones: the last third of a bull market is often the most dramatic - so acceleration filters should not be allowed to veto strong late-stage moves.

strategy_name: 10-month / 200-day moving-average trend filter
mechanism: Smoothing through averaging separates the trend signal from noise; price above the slow average is a lower-frequency trend state than daily price action.
setup_summary: Long when price is above the 10-month (200-day equivalent) moving average; exit to safe harbor when price closes below it; evaluate monthly. On the S&P 500 1974-2013 the rule was in stocks 74% of the time with 49 trades (1.2/yr) - results comparable to 12-month absolute momentum but with ~60% more trades/whipsaw.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: close above the 10-month MA. Invalidation: close below the 10-month MA -> de-risk; whipsaw risk is higher than absolute momentum because averaging produces false crossings (Faber 2007 rule).
risk_geometry: Monthly evaluation; no stop/target; exit on the MA cross; compared head-to-head with absolute momentum in the book, which is preferred on transaction costs (0.83 vs 1.2 trades/yr).
quote: One holds a long position when the price is above its 10-month moving average and exits the position when the price falls below the 10-month moving average.
chapter_anchor: Ch. 9, Mo' Better Momentum (Trend Following with Moving Averages)
notes: The slow-MA trend filter is the most widely-used crypto regime indicator (200-day SMA). V8-native use: alternative trend feature (price vs long-window MA) in the trend feature group, and a candidate regime filter; the book's comparison table is the falsifiable anchor - it shows MA timing is not superior to absolute momentum after costs, so prefer the trailing-return-sign feature and treat MA as a robustness check. Also caution: the book notes the 10-month length is itself a data-mined historical favorite (Brock et al., Siegel, Faber).

strategy_name: Behavioral drivers of momentum persistence
mechanism: Anchoring/underreaction delays price discovery, the disposition effect sells winners early and holds losers, and herding/positive-feedback later overextends - together they produce the initial-underreaction-then-delayed-overreaction pattern that keeps trends persisting.
setup_summary: Testable mechanism claim (not a tradable setup): momentum continuation is strongest where anchoring, herding and the disposition effect are strongest; e.g., retail-heavy markets (crypto perps) should exhibit at least as much serial correlation in trailing-return continuation as institutional markets. The book cites Odean (1998): disposition effect costs individual investors ~4.4%/yr.
trigger_invalidation: N/A - mechanism hypothesis, not a trigger. Falsifiable via the persistence of the momentum anomaly on fresh data and its strength in retail-dominated venues.
risk_geometry: None stated - this is the causal rationale for the trend_following family, not a setup.
quote: In anchoring, investors are slow to react to new information, which leads initially to underreaction. In herding, buying begets more buying and causes prices to overreact and move beyond fundamental value after the initial underreaction. strategy_name: Swing high/low trend analysis ('123') with objective swing significance and ADX filter
mechanism: price moving in higher highs/higher lows (bull) or lower highs/lower lows (bear) persists; breaking the first swing point in the trend direction guarantees a new swing extreme, so entry needs only three of the four pivot points
setup_summary: Objectively define swing highs/lows (a bar whose high is above the bar on each side; significance = number of bars to the left, 3-bar highs/lows treated as significant, 1-2 bar ignored - DeMark-derived). Long when a higher low is confirmed and price breaks the first swing high; short on the mirror. Stop at the most recent significant swing low/high, trailed to each new swing point; exit when the market returns to neutral. Take trades only when ADX is higher than the prior day (filter claimed to cut ~half of losers while keeping ~95% of winners).

Invalidated when the recent significant swing low/high is hit, or the market transitions to neutral (e.g., higher low after lower highs = megaphone/no-trade zone).
risk_geometry: Entry: stop order at the first swing point (breakout entry). Stop: most recent 3-bar swing high (shorts) / low (longs), trailed to each new swing extreme. No fixed R-target; exit on neutral transition or trailing stop. Stops intentionally wide - 'only stopped out when we are wrong' and only on significant moves.
quote: Go long when the market turns into a bull market, go short when the market turns into a bear market, and stand aside when the market is in any other condition.

strategy_name: Bishop exit - ADX trend-exhaustion liquidation signal

strategy_name: Conqueror - three-timeframe moving-average confluence with adaptive ATR stop
mechanism: a move is only tradable when short (10d), medium (10d MA momentum) and long (40d) trend readings are aligned; sitting out until all three agree avoids whipsaw, and an adaptive stop that tightens as conditions weaken gives a strong reward-to-risk ratio
setup_summary: Compute three conditions: (1) close minus 10-day MA of close, (2) 10-day MA minus 10-day MA 10 days ago, (3) close minus close 40 days ago. Long if all three positive, short if all three negative, stand aside otherwise. Entry at the close of the triggering bar. Stop: disaster stop sized to a fixed $2,000 loss, plus 2x ATR above the lowest close in the move (Conqueror I; 12x ATR for Conqueror II), reduced by one-third each time one condition flips sign; re-enter only after a condition flips positive then negative again. Backtest (Freeburg/CTCR 1972-1998, 4 currencies): 46% profitable trades, avg win/avg loss ratio 3.31, avg trade +$1,580.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: all three conditions same sign. Invalidated when the reduced ATR stop is hit, or the money-management stop; sideways markets never trigger all-three alignment, so the system sits out.
risk_geometry: Entry: close of the day all three conditions align. Stop: 2x ATR above lowest close (trailing), cut by 1/3 per flipped condition; disaster stop fixed $2,000. No target - exits on stop/tightening or re-alignment logic; notable for using a different exit technique than entry (rare).
quote: Go long if all three conditions are positive. Go short if all three conditions are negative. Stand aside on any other condition.

strategy_name: Stochastic divergence - daily (countertrend) vs weekly (trend change) with quantified lead times
mechanism: when price makes a new extreme close but stochastics (%K/%D) do not, momentum is weaker than price - the move is at risk of reversal; divergence magnitude scales with timeframe
setup_summary: Divergence = new price extreme (measured close-to-close) not confirmed by stochastics. Daily divergence predicts a short countertrend move: study of 58 daily divergences across ~30 futures found mean lead 4.5 days (SD 5.7) but mode 1 and median 2 days, mean retracement 5.9% (median 5%). Weekly divergence predicts an intermediate-term trend change: 124 cases, mode = the exact turning week, mean lead 2.8 weeks, mean retracement 15.3% (max 80%). Use daily divergence to trim 1/4 to 1/2 of a position, weekly divergence to exit longs / enter shorts aggressively on a reversal bar; Lane's stop = two bars below the two previous lows.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: unconfirmed new price extreme on stochastics. Invalidated if the divergence fails (the %K resumes the original direction - 'failure' signal, which the book trades WITH the trend); lead time is noisy, so a standalone divergence buy/sell is not mechanical without a confirmation bar.
risk_geometry: No fixed entry/exit: used as a partial-profit overlay on trend positions or as entry timing with a reversal-bar confirmation. Stop: low of the countertrend move (author) / two bars below two previous lows (Lane). Countertrend expected window 1-5 days (daily).
quote: In other words, the momentum of the price is less strong than the price itself.

strategy_name: Inside day (bar) breakout - one-bar consolidation breakout with lemonade reversal
mechanism: an inside bar is a day of balance; following whoever wins the breakout of the inside bar's range captures short-term directional momentum
setup_summary: An inside bar has high < prior bar's high and low > prior bar's low (whole range inside prior bar). Place a buy stop above the inside bar's high and a sell stop below its low; on fill, stop at the opposite side of the inside bar and exit at the close of the breakout bar. Book claims ~55% win rate with average winner much larger than loser. Enhancement - 'lemonade' trade (a failed signal is a signal): when the initial fill is stopped, reverse to the opposite side for a claimed 70-75% win rate; multiunit tactic: take 20 pips on one unit, hold the rest to the close.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: price trades through an inside bar extreme after the bar completes. Invalidated when the opposite inside-bar extreme is hit (stop); position exits at close of the breakout bar regardless of P&L.
risk_geometry: Entry: buy/sell stop at the inside bar extremes (breakout entry). Stop: opposite inside-bar extreme (contained risk = inside bar range). Exit: close of the breakout day (same-day hold); 20-40 pip quick-profit variant via multiunit tactic.
quote: An inside day is any day that has its whole range inside the range of the previous day.

strategy_name: Reversal day - trend-resumption reversal bar with trend filter
mechanism: a bar that makes an extreme beyond the prior bar yet closes back through it shows the prior trend's counter-move has failed and the dominant trend is reasserting (bullish = lower low + higher close; bearish = higher high + lower close)
setup_summary: Bullish reversal day = lower low than the prior bar AND closes higher; bearish = higher high AND closes lower. Enter at the close of the reversal bar, hold until the close of the next bar; stop below the bar's low (long) / above its high (short). Filter: take only in the direction of the prevailing trend - the reversal day marks the end of a short-term countertrend correction and resumption of the trend; also usable as a long-term entry (stop = three-bar low from trend analysis) and with the multiunit/quick-profit variant (20-40 pips).
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: reversal bar forms. Invalidated when the protective stop (bar extreme) is hit; then the lemonade reversal applies (rare for this method - most reversal-day trades are small winners, losses when stopped are larger than winners).
risk_geometry: Entry: close of the reversal bar (bar-close entry). Stop: below the bar's low / above its high, or a three-bar swing low for long-term use. Exit: close of the next day (or 20-40 pip quick profit).
quote: A Reversal Day occurs when a pair makes a lower low than the previous day and closes higher.

strategy_name: Maximum Excursion Analysis (MEA) - profit-target calibration from the MFE distribution
mechanism: after any signal, the maximum favorable excursion (MFE) follows a stable distribution; setting profit targets at percentile levels converts uncertain trend follow-through into high-probability partial targets and can turn losing signals profitable
setup_summary: For a given signal type (e.g., 55-day breakout), measure the maximum favorable excursion as a PERCENTAGE of price (not absolute pips) over a window, tabulate into a bell curve, and read off target probabilities - e.g., 'gains 100 pips 90% of the time, 200 pips 62%, 300 pips 32%'. Place a limit profit order at the chosen percentile target while keeping the entry stop. The book claims this principle can turn an unprofitable 5/10 MA-crossover system into a profitable one and generalizes the multiunit 'take a quick 20-pip profit' tactic.
trigger_invalidation: Target-level probabilities are instrument/regime-dependent - the bell curve must be re-estimated per pair and periodically; a target unreachable for the chosen percentile means the signal is a loser under the exit stop.
risk_geometry: Entry: original signal trigger. Exit: limit order at the MFE-percentile target; entry stop remains active. No fixed R-multiple - targets come from the empirical excursion distribution.

strategy_name: 5-0 harmonic pattern (failed-wave first-pullback reversal)
mechanism: A failed final impulse wave (nominally breaching the prior extreme) followed by an extreme 1.618-2.24 extension leg sets up the first pullback of a trend reversal; the 50% BC retracement pinpoints the D point.
setup_summary: On any timeframe: after an extended down move (X), price bounces to A, makes a failed-wave new low at B (XA extension 1.13-1.618, not above 2.24), rallies to C at a 1.618-2.24 extension of AB, then D = 50% retracement of BC converging with a Reciprocal AB=CD equal leg — a long entry at the first pullback of a reversal. Mirror for bearish. If BC never reaches 1.618 the structure is invalid.

strategy_name: BAMM (Bat Action Magnet Move) — CD-leg continuation after B-point break

setup_summary: Identify a Bat structure with B point at <=50% XA retracement; when the CD leg exceeds the B point (bullish breakout / bearish breakdown), trade the segment from the B-break to the pattern's PRZ completion (0.886 XA retracement) with the direction of the larger trend. strategy_name: Impulsive vs complex RSI extreme filter (extreme readings are not signals)

setup_summary: When RSI(14) tags below 30 or above 70, classify the structure: if it snaps back across the extreme line within 1-2 bars (impulsive), treat it as continuation of the predominant trend, not a reversal; only a complex W/M-type structure that persists at the extreme is a valid divergence-reversal starting point.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: RSI extreme reading (structure classification). Invalid: none as a trade — this is a filter; impulsive extremes explicitly do not warrant a reversal trade and may signal continuation.

strategy_name: Post-Event Directional Follow-Through Exit (candle-persistence hold)
mechanism: After a scheduled-event gap, the direction of the gap tends to persist while daily candles keep closing in the gap direction; the loser is discarded at the open and the winner is ridden until candle direction reverses or a hard 5-bar cap.

strategy_name: Buy new highs / sell new lows (X-day channel breakout)
mechanism: Strength follows strength: a market making new X-day highs tends to continue; the public's instinct to sell strength and await pullbacks is the losing habit.
setup_summary: Daily timeframe. When today's high exceeds the highest high of the last X days, buy on close; exit N bars later (13 days in the illustration) or at a fixed dollar stop ($3,500 in the test). Symmetric short on new X-day lows. Falsifiable: new-high breakouts carry positive expectancy; Williams asserts more money has been made buying new highs and selling new lows than with any other technique.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: high > highest high of prior X days. Invalidation: fixed dollar stop hit, or price falls back inside the prior range before the exit date (breakout fails).
risk_geometry: Entry on bar close after the new high; stop = fixed dollar ($3,500) or below prior structure; target = exit after fixed N bars (13), no fixed R target.
quote: more money has been made by buying new highs and selling new lows than with any other techniques known to traders.

strategy_name: Buy strong closes (close in upper portion of the day's range)
mechanism: A close near the high of the range signals demand control and continuation; strength is power a market needs to continue its trend.
setup_summary: Daily timeframe. If the close is in the upper 65% of the day's range, buy at that close and exit 5, 10, 15, or 20 days later with a protective stop. Symmetric: sell closes in the lower 35%. Falsifiable: strong-close momentum shows positive forward returns — reported to make money in all markets tested via System Writer.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: close within upper 65% of day's range. Invalidation: protective stop hit within the holding window; strength thesis dead if a subsequent close prints in the lower range.
risk_geometry: Entry at bar close; stop = protective (dollar); target = exit after fixed horizon (5/10/15/20 days), no fixed R target.
quote: If price today closed in the upper 65% of the day's range, what would happen if I bought on that close and exited 5, 10, 15, and 20 days later? ... In all markets, this basic strategy made money.

strategy_name: Trend systems: no protective stops, no fixed targets — let winners run
mechanism: A trend-following system's payoff comes from catching a few large trend moves; bolting on protective stops or fixed profit targets truncates those big wins and dampens accuracy and profit per trade.
setup_summary: For non-reversal (always-in-market, stop-and-reverse) trend-following systems, do not add money-management protective stops or fixed profit targets; exit only on trend reversal. Empirical claims over 20 years: a money-management stop cuts winning-trade percentage by 10-15% and average profit per trade by up to 1/3; fixed targets dampen system efficiency. Coffee system table: the $1,000 stop had $12,553 drawdown, the $4,500 stop $14,855 drawdown but made almost $30,000 more.
trigger_invalidation: The design is wrong for a given system if the majority of its profit comes from small wins rather than from a few large trend catches.
risk_geometry: Exit only at trend reversal (stop-and-reverse) or when the move tops/bottoms; no fixed R target; stop-and-reverse points intentionally wide.
quote: you cannot improve, appreciably, a good system by using targets ... effective commodity systems do better without a protective stop loss than with one—if they are not reversal systems.

strategy_name: Time creates profit — hold through pullbacks; longer timeframes have larger profit potential
mechanism: Large wins require time to mature; shortening the timeframe or exiting on early adverse pullbacks truncates the profit that large trend moves provide.
setup_summary: Falsifiable claim: profit scales with holding horizon — 'the longer a system's time frame, the greater the potential for a large profit.' Large trend moves contain substantial adverse pullbacks that must be endured; traders are typically shaken out just before the move resumes. Supporting practice: preframe equity dips and hold until the trend tops/bottoms or reaches major support.
trigger_invalidation: The hold-through-pullback prescription fails in trend-less regimes where adverse pullbacks convert winners to losers (regime dependence).
risk_geometry: Hold until the trend tops/bottoms or price reaches major support; exit on a bail-out indicator/system rather than mental discomfort; preframe equity dips.

strategy_name: Volatility breakout (range-expansion entry at period open)
mechanism: An explosive expansion of range sets a trend that persists until an equal/opposite expansion; entering at the next period open + X% of the reference range captures the continuation
setup_summary: Falsifiable: when a bar's range exceeds a reference (prior bar's range, or N-bar average range, or a swing-based measure) by a threshold, buy the next bar at open + X% of the reference range (short: open - X%). Williams' tests show adding the expansion to the NEXT bar's OPEN (not close or high) works best ($389 avg/trade across commodities); simple daily-range breakouts on bonds made $73,468 with 80% accuracy on 651 trades; restricting to best trade-days (buy Tue/Thu, sell Wed/Thu) cut trades in half and lifted avg/trade to $173 with 84% accuracy. Buy signals only after down days, sells after up days.
trigger_invalidation: Entry bar fails to extend (no follow-through beyond the entry level); or for longs, price falls back much below the entry-period open — a large-range up day seldom trades far below its open
risk_geometry: entry NEXT_BAR_OPEN + X% of reference range (X≈40-200% by day of week in tests; 50-100% common); stop = 50% of reference range subtracted from entry, or flat dollar stop ($1,500-2,500); target = bailout (first profitable opening) or period close; expiry = close of entry period or next 1-3 bars

strategy_name: Smash-day / specialists'-trap failed breakout of congestion, immediately reversed
mechanism: Public entries on an emotional breakout (naked close beyond a trading range); immediate reversal the next day means the breakout failed and the trapped flow becomes fuel for the opposite move
setup_summary: Falsifiable. Smash-day: a bar closes below the prior bar's low, often taking out the prior 3-8 bars' lows (a 'naked close'); if the very next bar trades back above that smash bar's high, the downside breakout failed — buy. Mirror for short. Specialists' trap: in an uptrend, 5-10 bars of sideways congestion break out with a naked close above the whole range; if the breakout bar's true low is broken within the next 1-3 days, the upside breakout was false — short (and vice versa for a buy trap). With day-of-week filtering (any day but Thursday) Williams reports 82-90% accuracy (bonds $420/trade avg; S&P outside-day-down-close pattern 85% on 109 occurrences).
trigger_invalidation: The smash/breakout bar's extreme is not retaken within 1-3 bars — the breakout is real and the thesis is dead
risk_geometry: entry: stop-order at the smash/breakout bar's opposite extreme on next-bar confirmation; stop: flat dollar ($1,500-2,000) or the breakout bar's extreme; target: first profitable opening (bailout); expiry: 1-3 bars
quote: The breakout is a magnet for the public to take action and they do. What kills them is the immediate reversal the very next day.

strategy_name: Ringed/swing-point market structure (nested short/intermediate/long-term highs and lows)
mechanism: A bar with lower highs on both sides is a short-term high (higher lows both sides = short-term low); nesting these produces intermediate and long-term structure; swing points are the only valid support/resistance and their violation signals trend change
setup_summary: Falsifiable mechanical definition (ignore inside days): short-term high = bar with lower highs on both sides; short-term low = bar with higher lows on both sides; intermediate = short-term point with higher/lower short-term points on both sides; long-term nested one more level. A short-term low is confirmed intra-period when price trades above the high of a bar with a lower low than the prior bar. Violation of a swing point is the trend-change trigger and stop reference; the (A)-type violation (break of the low preceding a failed new-high rally) is the stronger signal. Inside days (~7.6% of sessions) signal congestion — skip them; outside days (~7%) require intraday open-to-close study.
trigger_invalidation: Acceptance back through a retaken swing level without follow-through
risk_geometry: entry: on break of a swing level (stop order) or pullback to a swing level with trend confirmation; stop: beyond the swing point; target: next swing level; expiry: bar-based
quote: These points are the only valid support and resistance levels I have ever found.

strategy_name: Three-bar moving-average high/low pullback entry (swing-based variant of trend_pullback)
mechanism: In a swing-point-confirmed trend, buying the pullback to short-term support (3-bar MA of lows) and taking profits at the 3-bar MA of highs harvests mean-reversion-within-trend
setup_summary: Falsifiable intraday system (5-60 min bars): compute a 3-bar moving average of the highs and a 3-bar moving average of the lows. Only after the swing-point trend-flip confirms an uptrend, buy at the 3-bar MA-of-lows and take profits at the 3-bar MA-of-highs, awaiting pullbacks back to the low line; in a confirmed downtrend, short the 3-bar MA-of-highs and cover at the MA-of-lows. Pass on signals when the 3-bar low line would itself trigger a trend reversal. Williams reports 30+ consecutive winning trades with this approach.
trigger_invalidation: Swing-point trend flip in the opposite direction, or the 3-bar low line is violated by a trend reversal
risk_geometry: entry: limit at the 3-bar MA of lows (long) / 3-bar MA of highs (short); target: 3-bar MA of highs / lows (fixed structure, not R-multiple); stop: below the swing low / on trend flip; expiry: intraday bars
quote: The strategy is to buy at the price of the 3-bar moving average of the lows—if the trend is positive, according to the swing point trend identification technique—and take profits at the 3-bar moving average of the highs.

strategy_name: Will-Spread cross-market regime filter (primary/secondary ratio EMA cross)
mechanism: The spread ratio between a primary market and a causally-linked secondary market (bonds/gold, stocks/bonds) trends ahead of the primary market; an EMA-cross of the ratio across zero, confirmed by next-bar price action, marks the primary's regime
setup_summary: Falsifiable alignment tool: compute (primary price / secondary price) x 100; take a 5-period exponential minus a 20-period exponential of the spread (15-min/30-min bars; 3-vs-15 for S&P vs T-bills). Trade long when the oscillator crosses above zero AND the very next bar trades above the crossing bar's high; short on the mirror. Williams uses it to stay aligned with the true trend, not standalone; combined with the first-of-month window it produced 13 month-end trades in 1997 with 10 winners (+99.70 S&P points, $24,925), and it kept traders short through the 1987 crash ($46,000/contract) until the October 20 positive crossing. Underlying claims: higher bond prices are bullish for stocks; gold downtrend is bullish for bonds (gold uptrend impedes bond rallies).
trigger_invalidation: Zero-line crossing without next-bar confirmation = stand aside (unless other gauges align)
risk_geometry: entry: stop-order on next-bar confirmation of the zero-cross; stop: trailing through prior swing/volatility breakout level; target: opposite zero-cross or fixed 2-3 day window

strategy_name: Volume-Damped Pullback in Trend (Hold Rule)
mechanism: trend_continuation
setup_summary: While holding a position aligned with the trend, a counter-trend pullback develops on FALLING volume, and no stopping volume (rising volume with narrowing spreads) appears at the pullback extreme. Thesis: the pullback is a pause, not a reversal; hold through it. Applies symmetrically to long (pullbacks down) and short (pullbacks up) positions.
trigger_invalidation: Pullback candles show widening spreads with rising volume (stopping volume / absorption) at the pullback extreme; or a high-volume reversal candle reclaims the position entry zone.
risk_geometry: Entry N/A (position already open); stop beyond the pullback swing extreme; no new target; this rule governs holding, not entry.

strategy_name: Volume-Validated Congestion Breakout (Cause and Effect)
mechanism: range_expansion_release
setup_summary: Price builds an extended congestion zone defined by pivot highs/lows; below-average volume confirms the range. Trigger: a bar closes clearly beyond the ceiling (or floor) with above-average, preferably rising volume. Stop below the last pivot low (or above last pivot high) on the entry side. Cause-and-effect: the longer the congestion, the longer the post-breakout trend should last.
trigger_invalidation: Breakout candle closes back inside the range; breakout occurs on low/falling volume (trap); retest of the breached level fails to hold.
risk_geometry: Entry NEXT_BAR_CLOSE after the breakout close; stop beyond the last pivot low/high; target range-height projection or next structure; expiry scaled by congestion duration.

strategy_name: Volume-Collapse Trend Exhaustion (Exit Rule)
mechanism: exhaustion_gravity
setup_summary: In a mature multi-week trend, price keeps printing wide-range bars in the trend direction while volume collapses toward near-zero (market makers pushing price with no participation), OR a volume spike prints with no matching price progress. strategy_name: Triangle and Pennant Breakout with Volume Validation

strategy_name: The Pullback — stochastic-oversold + reversal-candle confirmed pullback in uptrend
mechanism: A dip in an established uptrend is temporary weakness (profit-taking or news noise); traders who missed the prior move re-enter on the dip, reasserting the dominant trend.
setup_summary: Uptrending stock (higher lows over >=3 months; 20MA>50MA both rising) pulls back to touch an upsloping 20 MA (strong trend) or 50 MA (weak trend); stochastics (5,3) drops to/below the 20 oversold line; the current daily candle is a bullish reversal (hammer, engulfing, piercing, or doji). All three conditions register a buy signal on the same day; confluence with an upsloping trendline under the lows improves odds. Daily chart, hold 3-30 days.
trigger_invalidation: Invalid if the pullback closes below the 50 MA, violates the uptrend trendline, shows bearish indicator divergence, or prints a double top; a red/black candle on the day is a wait-and-see condition (recheck next day).
risk_geometry: Entry: stop order $0.02-0.05 above prior day's intraday high (gaps -> limit order; if never hit, scratch); stop: below swing support / 2xATR, max -8% (typ 5-6%); target: 1.5-2.0x stop or 3xATR, or trailing on closing basis; expiry: 3-30 days.
quote: Normally after a period of minor weakness—as measured here by the stochastics indicator reaching an oversold level—the dominant uptrend will reassert itself as traders who missed out on the prior move use the dip to get on board.

strategy_name: The Relief Rally — bearish mirror of the pullback (short rally into MA resistance)
mechanism: A rally in a downtrend is a short-term reevaluation (profit-taking, short squeeze, or news); when it fails at moving-average resistance the dominant downtrend resumes.

Three factors register a sell-short signal; confluence with a downsloping trendline over the highs improves odds. Best in bearish strongly/weakly trending regimes.

strategy_name: The Coiled Spring — bull flag/pennant tightening-range breakout
mechanism: Strong stocks consolidate sideways after a runup instead of selling off; the tightening range (coil) stores energy that releases in a burst of upward momentum when it springs open.
setup_summary: Weakly-to-strongly uptrending stock (20MA>50MA) puts in a new high that is at least a 3-month high within the past 20 trading days, then consolidates in a tightening range lasting 7-20 trading days (coil): sideways-to-slightly-down, trading range getting smaller, no part of the coil extending to/below the 50 MA (tails may poke out if candle bodies stay inside). Pure pattern play — no oscillators needed, only 20/50 MAs and trendlines. Buy signal: close breaks the trendline over the tops of the coil; close below the lower trendline negates.
trigger_invalidation: Invalidated by a close below the lower coil trendline; coils longer than 20 days signal indecision and are avoided; range must be tightening (lows getting higher and/or highs lower); candle bodies must stay in the coil.

strategy_name: Bullish Base Breakout — contrarian accumulation-base breakout after downtrend
mechanism: A sideways base at the bottom of a downtrend, confirmed by rising momentum (MACD higher lows) and accumulation (OBV trendline break), flips supply into demand and triggers a rally.
setup_summary: Downtrending stock (lower highs; 20MA below falling 50MA) has traded sideways for >=30 trading days in a consolidation base (flat/falling rectangle or symmetrical/ascending/descending triangle; rising wedge explicitly invalid) at the bottom of the downtrend; MACD prints a series of higher lows within the base; OBV rises above a trendline over its tops. Buy signal = first green candle after the OBV trendline break (or on the OBV-break day if that candle is green). Contrarian: works in bullish-weak, bearish-strong/weak, and range-bound markets; often seen in lower-priced stocks.
trigger_invalidation: A rising wedge base is invalid (usually precedes continuation of the downtrend); no buy without OBV accumulation confirmation — price breaking out of the base without the OBV signal is not a valid entry.
risk_geometry: Entry: day of/after OBV trendline break on a green candle; stop: below base low / 2xATR; target: quick +10% burst within days or trailing for +20-30% in 6-7 weeks; examples AKS +20% in 7 days, KLAC +19% (trailing), JNPR +30% in 6 weeks.
quote: To render the setup valid, we need the indicators to tell us two things about price behavior within the base: it has to be gaining in momentum, and there must be evidence that shares are under accumulation.
chapter_anchor: Ch. 9 'The Bullish Base Breakout' (pp. 181-189)
notes: Reuses starter slug breakout_retest (V8 backlog family location,volatility,history) but adds participation features (OBV trendline break + MACD higher lows) not currently in the backlog spec — a candidate FEATURE_INPUT for the participation group. Classic antecedent is the Darvas box (Introduction, pp. 3-7): buy break of box top, raise box on new range, exit on break of box bottom. 'OBV often leads price': price frequently follows an OBV breakout.
