strategy_name: Bullish/Bearish Indicator Divergence at deep pullback or sharp rally
mechanism: Price making new extremes without oscillator confirmation shows waning momentum; divergence foreshadows a reversal toward the direction of the indicators, which align with the larger trend.
setup_summary: Bullish: stock in a long-range uptrend (50 MA above a RISING 200 MA) trades below the 50 MA and puts in >=2 clear price lows >=5 trading days apart; the last price low pairs with a HIGHER low in >=2 of {MACD, MACD histogram, stochastics, RSI, OBV, CCI}; a bullish reversal candle triggers the buy. Bearish mirror: long-range downtrend (50 MA below a FALLING 200 MA), price above the 50 MA, >=2 higher highs, last high pairs with a LOWER high in >=2 indicators, bearish candle triggers the short. Confluence with 200 MA / trendline / prior support-resistance improves odds. Works in range-bound and weak-trend markets.
trigger_invalidation: Too many lower lows (bullish) eventually negate the long-range uptrend and nullify the setup (likewise too many higher highs bearish); the 50MA/200MA relationship is the regime gate — 50 MA crossing under the 200 MA negates the long-range uptrend even with a rising 200 MA.
risk_geometry: Entry: day of bullish/bearish reversal candle, or next day via stop above/below prior day's extreme; stop: below last low / support or 2xATR, max -8%; target: 1.5-2.0x stop or trailing; examples FWLT +25% in 20 days; BRCM +40% over two trades vs +24% buy-and-hold.
quote: Whenever price sets a higher high or lower low without the indicators following suit, we have a setup that often foreshadows large market moves.
chapter_anchor: Ch. 9 'The Bullish Divergence' (pp. 170-175) + Ch. 10 'The Bearish Divergence' (pp. 198-203)
notes: Reuses starter slug rsi_divergence (multi-indicator momentum divergence family). Carr calls it 'a real workhorse... we can use it in all sorts of markets, even bearish ones.' Falsifiable spec: 50MA vs 200MA slope defines the long-range regime; >=2 of six oscillators diverging, >=5 bars between lows; strong divergence (much lower price low + much higher indicator low) and >2 diverging indicators favored. Implementable from PIT oscillator history (feature group: history). This is a new V8 behavior family; would enter the registry and compete for one of the 3 active Expert slots.
book: Trend Trading for a Living - Learn the Skills and Gain the Confidence to Trade for a Living 2007

strategy_name: The Gap Down — contrarian short after an unfilled gap down in a steady uptrend
mechanism: An unfilled gap down in an uptrend is a trend killer: panic and profit-locking inverts the dynamic; dip-buyers get trapped, and a break below the gap-day low releases them into a sharp drop.
setup_summary: Stock in a steady uptrend (price above a rising 50 MA for at least the past 40 trading days; 50 MA rising without major dips) prints an UNFILLED gap-down candle: at the close, the day's intraday high remains below the prior day's intraday low. Sell-short signal triggers anytime after the gap-down day when price trades below the intraday low of the gap-down candle. Best in bullish-strong, bullish-weak, and range-bound markets; the gap must follow a significant (>=3-month) new high.
trigger_invalidation: Setup negated if price trades up into the gap prior to triggering the sell signal; avoid 'safe-haven' stocks making new highs in a bear market; favor above-average volume on the gap day and prior resistance / bearish divergence at the preceding high.
risk_geometry: Entry: stop order below the gap-day intraday low (or next bar); stop: above the gap / swing high; target: trailing stop; examples EBAY (double gap down then breakdown), SWIR (long gap candle, drop resumed after 3 days); warning — never buy a dip to support after an unfilled gap down, 'you are likely to get caught in a bull trap.'
quote: Never underestimate the power of a gap down. It is truly a trend killer.
chapter_anchor: Ch. 10 'The Gap Down' (pp. 203-207)
notes: The unfilled-gap observable is equity-specific (overnight close-to-open discontinuity); 24/7 perp crypto has no exchange gaps, though sudden wick/candle failures (post-funding dumps, flash-crash wicks) are analogs. Gate on whether a 'gap' can be defined on 1h BTCUSDT bars and on V8's simulator gap semantics (the sim models equity-style gaps). The bull-trap warning ('never buy a dip to support after an unfilled gap down') is a transferable RISK filter for the trend_pullback family: do not take pullback longs when the pullback began with a gap-down / high-velocity downside candle.
book: Trend Trading for a Living - Learn the Skills and Gain the Confidence to Trade for a Living 2007

strategy_name: Rising Wedge Breakdown — distribution-wedge short with OBV/MACD confirmation
mechanism: Narrowing oscillations in an uptrend with slowing momentum (MACD lower highs) and distribution (OBV trendline break) exhaust the rally; the OBV break leads the price breakdown.
setup_summary: Uptrending stock (strong or weak) oscillates in a narrowing wedge: support and resistance trendlines under the lows / over the highs each need >=3 price-point touches (not pivots, just bar touches); MACD makes a series of lower highs inside the wedge; OBV falls below a trendline under its lows. Sell-short signal = first red/black candle after the OBV trendline break (may enter before price itself breaks the wedge). Contrarian; works in bullish-weak/strong and range-bound markets.
trigger_invalidation: No signal without OBV distribution confirmation; fewer than 3 touches per wedge trendline invalid; ascending-triangle (flat-top) wedges are less favored than rising wedges; >2 of RSI/CCI/OBV falling during the wedge favored, and more red than green candles.
risk_geometry: Entry: close of the OBV-trigger day; stop: above wedge top / 2xATR; target: trailing stop; NVDA +30% in ~4 weeks (OBV trigger preceded the price breakdown); CSCO +17% over 2 months, entry 20.75 before price closed below the wedge.
quote: MACD must be making a series of lower highs while price is within the wedge... OBV must fall below a trendline placed under the lows of the indicator.
chapter_anchor: Ch. 10 'The Rising Wedge Breakdown' (pp. 213-219)
notes: Short mirror of the bullish base breakout with distribution (not accumulation) confirmation. Consistency note across the book: the rising wedge is explicitly REJECTED as a valid base in the bullish setup (precedes downtrend continuation) but IS the valid pattern here — i.e., rising wedge = bearish in both chapters. The OBV-break-leads-price mechanic ('price often follows an OBV breakout' / 'you often will be in at the very start of a significant trend-down sell-off') is a participation-feature timing signal.
book: Trend Trading for a Living - Learn the Skills and Gain the Confidence to Trade for a Living 2007

strategy_name: Market Regime -> Setup-Class Selection (five market types from 20/50 MA slope)
mechanism: Market state (strong/weak trend or range, plus how long it has persisted) determines which setup class carries the edge: breakouts in strong trends, continuation/pullback plays in weak trends, reversals in ranges.
setup_summary: Classify the market into five states from the 20/50 MA slope, separation, and pullback depth: bullish-strong (20MA>50MA both rising, distance large/growing, pullbacks only to 20MA), bullish-weak (50MA rising, 20MA fluctuating, pullbacks reach the 50MA), bearish-strong (mirror: 20MA<50MA both falling, rallies only to 20MA), bearish-weak (mirror: rallies reach the 50MA), range-bound (20MA spends about as much time above as below a mostly-flat 50MA, price passes through both). Then trade the matching class: breakout/breakdown plays in strong trends, pullback/continuation in weak trends, reversal plays in ranges. The longer a market persists in its current state, the shorter the intended holding period and targets. General-market gauge: slope of the 50-day MA of the S&P 500.
trigger_invalidation: Regime re-classification on MA slope/cross events (e.g., 20MA crossing 50MA, 50MA rolling over); a 'snakey' fluctuating 20MA with flat 50MA is the range-bound tell; a tight range is next to impossible to profit from except by day traders — in that state move to instruments/stocks showing sizeable moves.
risk_geometry: N/A — regime gate that determines which expert families are admissible per bar (a pre-filter, not an entry).
quote: In weak uptrends and downtrends, you should focus on continuation plays; in strong uptrends and downtrends, you should focus on breakout plays; and in range-bound markets, you should look for reversal setups.
chapter_anchor: Ch. 4 habit 6 (pp. 86-87) + Ch. 7 'Determining General Market Direction' (pp. 113-131)
notes: Directly implementable on 1h BTCUSDT bars from MA slopes — no wall-clock dependency, preserves determinism. This is the missing gating layer in V8: which Expert families are admissible depends on regime state (not a scorer, not a ranker — a deterministic admission filter). Motivation: BTTT-MAX (Introduction, pp. 21-23), a fully-invested hourly MA-crossover system, made >500% in 2000's extreme volatility but profits dried up when conditions changed — pure momentum without a regime gate is regime-dependent. Supporting stat: 'Up to 80 percent of the time, stocks move sideways; they run in trends only about 20 percent of the time' (Ch. 5, p. 100) — range-state must be handled explicitly. Carr's caveat: chart-specific selection trumps market direction ('the vital key is finding the best-looking chart').
book: Trend Trading for a Living - Learn the Skills and Gain the Confidence to Trade for a Living 2007

strategy_name: Volume climax reversal (buying/selling climax)
mechanism: a high-volume, wide-range bar at a trend extreme that closes at the open exhausts the dominant side; the deep wick shows the opposite side absorbed the flow, setting up trend reversal.
setup_summary: At the end of an extended trend (after a distribution phase at a top, or an accumulation phase at a bottom), price prints one to three repeated bars with high or ultra-high volume, a deep wick and a narrow body, closing at or near the open. Selling climax (deep upper wick, high volume, top of a bull trend) precedes a fast break lower; buying climax (deep lower wick, high volume, bottom of a waterfall) precedes a march higher. Entry comes only after the climax is confirmed by subsequent price action, never on the signal bar itself.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: climax bar at a trend extreme with well-above-average volume closing at/near the open. Invalidation: volume below average (not a climax), the candle appears mid-trend rather than at an extreme, or follow-through continues in the trend direction on rising volume (no reversal).
risk_geometry: Book gives no stop/target; it stresses the oil-tanker effect - do not enter on the signal bar, wait for follow-through. Natural stops: below the buying-climax low / above the selling-climax high.
quote: Here we will see high volume coupled with a candlestick which has a deep upper wick and narrow body, and is one of the most powerful combinations of price action and volume we will ever see on a chart.
chapter_anchor: Ch.5 - The Selling Climax / The Buying Climax
notes: Extends the existing DATA_BLOCKED capitulation backlog family (mechanism capitulation_exhaustion) with the symmetric selling-climax variant and the explicit close-at-open + deep-wick + high-volume bar spec. In crypto perps, liquidation cascades produce the waterfall/climax signature naturally; no exchange gaps means the 'break lower fast' leg is continuous.
book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis 2013

strategy_name: Low-volume test of supply/demand (Wyckoff test)
mechanism: after accumulation/distribution, a probe back into the old heavy-volume zone that closes near the open on low volume proves the opposite side has been absorbed, so the campaign can proceed and breakout is imminent.
setup_summary: After an accumulation phase (bottom) or distribution phase (top), price is marked back into the recent heavy-selling/heavy-buying zone (test of supply / test of demand). A successful test: narrow body, deep wick toward the tested zone, closes near the open, LOW volume - residual sellers/buyers are gone and the next move is the breakout. A failed test (high volume, close-through) means the campaign must return into the zone for more mopping-up; no entry.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: test bar into an old high-volume zone after an accumulation/distribution phase closes near the open on low volume. Invalidation: high-volume close-through of the test zone (failed test), or no prior accumulation/distribution phase (test has no meaning).
risk_geometry: Book specifies the candle form (narrow body, deep lower wick, colour unimportant, low volume) but no stop/target; entry is after the successful test is confirmed, before/at the breakout leg.
quote: If the volume remains low, this instantly tells the insiders that there are few sellers left, and that virtually all the selling has been absorbed in the accumulation phase of the campaign.
chapter_anchor: Ch.5 - Testing Supply / Testing Demand
notes: Distinct from liquidity_sweep_reclaim: this is a low-volume probe closing near the open, not a wick-through-reclaim. Works on any timeframe; in 24/7 crypto the test can occur without a news catalyst.
book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis 2013

strategy_name: Volume-validated congestion breakout with low-volume retest (fake-out detection)
mechanism: moving out of a congestion zone requires effort; a breakout on well-above-average rising volume is genuine and the broken level becomes support/resistance, while a breakout on low volume is an insider trap (fake-out).
setup_summary: Define a congestion zone from isolated pivot highs/lows (3-bar patterns). A valid breakout: a clean close beyond the ceiling/floor (clear water, not an intra-bar touch) on well-above-average, rising volume. After the break, a pullback to test the broken level on LOW/falling volume confirms and is the entry. A breakout on LOW volume is a fake-out/trap - stand aside. Applies to continuation and reversal breakouts alike.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: pivot-defined congestion; close beyond the level on above-average rising volume. Invalidation: breakout bar on low/falling volume (fake-out), or retest of the broken level on rising volume (breakdown), or no clean close beyond the level.
risk_geometry: Book: 'any stop loss could then be placed in the lower regions of the price congestion' (the broken zone becomes natural protection); targets are the next volume-dense congestion platforms; a 'clear water' close beyond the level is required.
quote: A break out from such a price area on low volume, is a classic trap move by the insiders, and is often referred to as a 'fake out'.
chapter_anchor: Ch.7 - Support And Resistance Explained
notes: Refines the DATA_BLOCKED breakout_retest backlog family with two hard rules the book stresses: (1) volume must be above average and rising on the breakout bar, (2) retest must be on low/falling volume. No-gap 24/7 crypto means breakouts unfold continuously rather than on gapped opens.
book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis 2013

strategy_name: Dynamic pivot trend entry/exit (trend management via isolated pivots)
mechanism: after a volume-validated breakout, an intact higher-high/higher-low sequence of isolated pivot bars defines a live trend; a pivot that fails to exceed the prior one signals the trend is pausing or reversing, triggering exit - enabling entry near the start of a trend rather than after it is obvious.
setup_summary: Following a volume-validated breakout from congestion, hold the position while the market posts isolated pivot highs/lows (3-bar patterns) in sequence: for an uptrend, pivot highs above prior pivot highs and pivot lows above prior pivot lows confirm and hold. Exit when a pivot high posts at or below the prior pivot high (or a pivot low at/below the prior), signalling a secondary congestion phase or reversal. Works symmetrically for downtrends (lower lows/lower highs; exit on a higher pivot low).
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: first pivot after a volume-validated breakout. Invalidation: pivots fail to build a sequential pattern (market lacking momentum - 'if these are missing... the market is potentially weak'), or a break the opposite way through the pivot structure (trend reversal, exit).
risk_geometry: Position held through minor pullbacks while the pivot sequence is intact; exit on pivot-sequence failure; no explicit stop/target - pivots themselves are the waypoints. Higher-TF context determines pause vs reversal.
quote: we see a pivot high posted that is lower or perhaps at the same level as a previous pivot, and it is at this point that we are looking at a market that is perhaps moving into a secondary congestion phase
chapter_anchor: Ch.8 - Dynamic Trends And Trend Lines
notes: Directly usable as a still_valid/exit rule for trend-following experts (candidate refinement of trend_pullback exit or a new lifecycle rule): the pivot-sequence failure is a deterministic, bar-data-only exit trigger.
book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis 2013

strategy_name: Cause-and-effect: consolidation duration/depth scales trend extent
mechanism: Wyckoff's law of cause and effect: the size of the 'cause' (duration and volume of accumulation/distribution congestion) is directly proportional to the size of the 'effect' (the extent of the ensuing trend).
setup_summary: Markets spend roughly 70% of the time in sideways congestion; trends are born from congestion. Measure the duration and depth of a congestion phase (bars and volume density) and use it as a prior for the extent of the following trend: the longer and deeper the congestion, the larger the expected move after the volume-validated breakout (cause large, effect large; cause small, effect small). Also applies across timeframes (nested Russian-doll cycles).
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: completed congestion phase followed by volume-validated breakout. Invalidation: congestion that resolves back into the range (no breakout) or a breakout that fails on volume; the proportionality is a tendency, not a guarantee - each market has its own tempo.
risk_geometry: None stated; used for expectation-setting (how far a trend may run) and choosing minor-vs-primary trend, not for stop/target arithmetic.
quote: If the cause is large, then the effect will be large as well. If the cause is small, then the effect will also be small.
chapter_anchor: Ch.1 - Wyckoff's Laws; Ch.5 - The Accumulation/Distribution Phases
notes: Falsifiable via measurement (consolidation width/duration vs. subsequent trend extent) on perp history; could also inform a simulator prior for trend extent. Corroborated by the Wyckoff line of books in this library.
book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis 2013

strategy_name: Accumulation/distribution phase detection (campaign regime filter)
mechanism: before a major move, large operators accumulate (buying during engineered sell-offs) or distribute (selling into manufactured demand) inside a range; the volume signature of absorbed high-volume moves reveals which campaign is running, so a trend-start can be anticipated from the regime rather than after the trend.
setup_summary: During a sideways range, repeated high-volume sell-offs that close as narrow-spread candles (absorption, not follow-through) followed by quiet recovery = accumulation regime; repeated high-volume up-rallies that stall in a narrow range = distribution regime. These phases precede the next trend, in all timeframes. Regime label (accumulation / distribution / neutral) from volume-absorption patterns gates trend-start expectations and prepares for the low-volume test and breakout.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: range-bound price with absorbing (narrow-spread, high-volume) counter-trend bars. Invalidation: an absorption bar that fails to hold (price breaks the range on rising volume in the campaign direction before the test/breakout), or insufficient duration (a few bars of whipsaw is not a phase).
risk_geometry: None - regime classification; entry still requires the test/breakout triggers (low-volume-test and breakout_retest findings).
quote: These areas are the breeding grounds for trends.
chapter_anchor: Ch.5 - The Accumulation Phase / The Distribution Phase; Ch.8 - summary
notes: Propose as a regime filter on the 1h perp tape (range-detection + volume-absorption labels) that gates the breakout/retest and low-volume-test experts; the 'insider' narrative is not testable, but the volume-absorption signature is.
book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis 2013

strategy_name: Support/resistance role reversal: broken level flips and is retested (breakout retest)
mechanism: Once price breaks a level, the old level flips polarity (resistance becomes demand, support becomes supply) and the retest attracts flow in the breakout direction
setup_summary: After a breakout above resistance, a pullback that holds at the old level (now support) is a long; after a break below support, a rally into the old level (now resistance) is a short. Book cases: MEOH May 8 decline back to April peaks where 'support and resistance reversed roles. Buyers stepped in at support'; WOLF June 5-14 where 'Prior resistance had become new support'; S/R is flexible, not a hard line.
trigger_invalidation: Retest fails if price closes back through the flip level (breakout fails / false breakout); the book's glossary defines false breakout as a close beyond a level without momentum to continue, followed by reversal.
risk_geometry: Entry on the retest rejection candle close; stop beyond the flip level; target = measured move or next structure; the flip level's strength is judged by prior swing history.
quote: As they often do, support and resistance reversed roles. Buyers stepped in at support (6) and pushed price back up to close well off the low as the long lower shadow indicates.
chapter_anchor: Ch. 11 Case Study 2 (MEOH #6), Case Study 3 (WOLF #5); Ch. 10 Fig 10.7 (FLR support from prior April-May minor peaks); Glossary False breakout
notes: Directly corroborates V8's existing DATA_BLOCKED backlog family breakout_retest (requires location, volatility, history); 24/7 perp trading gives many clean level-flips and liquidation cascades often mark them.
book: Getting Started in Candlestick Charting 2008

strategy_name: Capitulation / selling climax and blow-off top: extreme-volume thrusts that end moves
mechanism: Extreme volume during a sharp thrust exhausts the move's fuel; the climax is frequently followed by a trend change
setup_summary: Capitulation: a sharp decline on very high volume with panic selling, often followed by a change in trend direction (long). Blow-off top: a sharp upward thrust in an uptrend on heavy volume followed by aggressive selling, often a trend change (short). Selling climax is the mirror of the blow-off. The climax needs genuinely extreme volume to count.
trigger_invalidation: Volume must be truly extreme (climax); if the sharp move continues the climax thesis is invalid; a climax without a subsequent reversal candle is just high-volume continuation.
risk_geometry: Entry after the climax reversal candle closes (e.g., hammer on heavy volume, SUN #8); stop beyond the climax extreme; target = mean/prior range.
quote: True capitulation involves very high volume and a sharp decline as panic selling occurs. Capitulation is often followed by a change in the direction of the trend.
chapter_anchor: Glossary (Capitulation, Blow-off top, Selling climax)
notes: Directly corroborates V8's DATA_BLOCKED backlog family capitulation (mechanism capitulation_exhaustion, requires trend, volatility, history); in crypto perps the analog is a liquidation cascade (deleveraging) with taker-volume spike.
book: Getting Started in Candlestick Charting 2008

strategy_name: Overextension fade: price too far from the moving average + oscillator extreme = vulnerable to pullback
mechanism: Price stretched beyond its short-term mean loses tensile energy; overextension makes counter-move reversal signals valid even when the candlestick is non-ideal
setup_summary: When price has moved 'a good distance away from the moving average' (20-SMA in the cases) with the stochastic at an extreme, reversal signals fire with normal-to-high validity. SUN #4: a non-ideal dark cloud cover after a large run from the 20-SMA with overbought stochastic was 'just as strong as an ideal pattern'. WOLF #6: after moving up from the average price was 'vulnerable to a pullback'. Shrinking real bodies (spinning tops) toward the end of an upswing flagged the same exhaustion (SUN #7).
trigger_invalidation: In a persistent trend, overextension can extend further; the fade thesis requires S/R context and a reversal candle, not distance alone.
risk_geometry: Entry at the reversal close; stop beyond the overextension swing; target = the moving average / mean.
quote: Since price had moved a good distance away from the moving average, and the stochastic oscillator was in overbought territory, the signal was just as strong as an ideal pattern.
chapter_anchor: Ch. 11 Case Study 1 (SUN #4, #7), Case Study 3 (WOLF #6); Index 'Overextended stocks, 143'
notes: Best framed as a gating feature (distance-from-mean + oscillator extreme) for the candlestick-reversal families rather than a standalone fade: fading overextension in strong crypto trends without a level is dangerous.
book: Getting Started in Candlestick Charting 2008

strategy_name: Three-bar star reversal (morning star / evening star)
mechanism: Staged sentiment flip: a long one-sided body, then a small-body star gapped away from it (momentum stall), then a strong opposite body closing deeply into the first body (control seized).
setup_summary: After a decline, bar 1 is a long bearish body; bar 2 gaps down (bodies do not touch; shadows may overlap) forming a small body or doji star; bar 3 is a strong bullish body that closes deeply into bar 1's body (morning star; evening star is the mirror after an advance). Heavy volume on bar 3 strengthens the signal; a doji star is a stronger variant.
trigger_invalidation: If bar 3 does not intrude deeply into bar 1 the signal is weak/invalid; bodies of bars 2-3 touching or overlapping are acceptable variations; patterns forming inside consolidation have little significance.
risk_geometry: Book flags that a very long bar 3 can leave an inadequate reward-to-risk ratio for entry upon completion (same for evening star); entry after pattern confirmation; stop at the pattern's failure point; targets from Western structure.
quote: The deeper the intrusion of the third candle's white real body into the first candle's black real body, the more likely a reversal, especially if the third session is accompanied by heavy volume.
chapter_anchor: Ch 3, Morning Star, pp.72-75
notes: Requires body gaps between consecutive bars; on continuous 1h crypto these body-gaps are frequent (no session close), so detection is feasible, but the gap semantics differ from session-based stock markets. Overlaps with engulfing when bar 3 fully engulfs the star; lower priority than the single/two-bar families.
book: Getting Started in Candlestick Charting 2008

strategy_name: Support-resistance role reversal and retest after breakout/breakdown
mechanism: Once a level is closed through, participants re-anchor expectations on the other side; prior resistance becomes support and its retest is a low-risk continuation entry.
setup_summary: After a close above resistance (breakout) or below support (breakdown), price pulls back and retests the broken level as support/resistance; the retest is the entry. The setup strengthens when the original breakout had heavy volume and the retest occurs on declining volume (acceptance of the new level). Role reversals also occur at broken trendlines and broken 50/200 MAs.
trigger_invalidation: If the retest fails (price closes back through the level), the polarity thesis is invalid and the event is reclassified as a failed breakout/breakdown. The book notes it is ambiguous at the right edge whether a range is consolidation or topping/bottoming until the close-through resolves it.
risk_geometry: Low-risk entry because the stop sits just below the retested level (failure point); the book explicitly says the retest 'offers traders a low-risk opportunity to get aboard the trend rather than chasing'. Breakout strategies often have no fixed target; the book's retest entries use trend continuation as the objective.
quote: It is very common for prior support to be tested as resistance after a breakdown, and vice versa after an upside breakout.
chapter_anchor: Ch 7, Reversion to the Mean, p.139; Ch 9, Support and Resistance Reverse Roles, pp.191-193
notes: Feeds the existing DATA_BLOCKED breakout_retest backlog family. Level polarity is observable in 24/7 crypto; retests on low volume map to the participation feature group. Multiple tests of a level strengthen it.
book: Getting Started in Candlestick Charting 2008

strategy_name: Volume confirmation of breakouts/reversals and price-volume trend relationships
mechanism: Volume is the force behind price moves: heavy volume on a breakout or reversal signal shows real participation and confirms it; a volume-less upside breakout is suspect (false breakout); a pullback on diminishing volume within a trend is profit-taking, not distribution, so the trend resumes.
setup_summary: Add volume features to entries/exits: require volume above its 20-30 period moving average on bullish reversal patterns and on upside breakouts; treat an upside breakout without volume expansion as suspect/false; treat a pullback on declining volume within an uptrend as a continuation opportunity (entry with a closer stop); flag price-volume divergence (price rising, volume declining) as trend weakening. Table 6.1 gives the four systematic states (rising/declining price x rising/declining volume).
trigger_invalidation: The book makes the volume rule asymmetric: downside breaks do not need heavy volume because 'the market can continue to fall under its own weight', so a single symmetric volume threshold would mis-filter shorts.
risk_geometry: Volume is a confirm/filter feature, not a risk parameter; this finding sets no entry/stop/target of its own.
quote: An upside breakout after a period of consolidation is usually accompanied by heavy volume. In fact, the breakout is suspect if not and may be a false breakout.
chapter_anchor: Ch 6, Analyzing Volume Patterns and Trends, p.103-105; Table 6.1
notes: Caution for perps: exchange-reported volume is aggregated and can be inflated or wash-traded, so use relative volume (vs its own MA) rather than absolute thresholds. The price-volume relationship table is a cheap, systematic feature set for the participation group.
book: Getting Started in Candlestick Charting 2008

strategy_name: Buy pullbacks in an uptrend / reversion-to-the-mean entry (don't chase overextension)
mechanism: Price deviates from the 20-period MA ('catching air') and tends to revert to the mean; pullbacks and basing within a trend are healthy rest stops, so entries near the MA offer a closer stop than chasing strength.
setup_summary: In an established uptrend (rising swing highs and lows, price mostly above the 20-SMA, a valid rising support trendline), wait for price to pull back to the 20/50-period MA or base sideways rather than buying strength; enter on the pullback so the initial protective stop can sit close. The 50/200-period MAs act as dynamic support/resistance. Inverse for downtrends: sell rallies to the MAs.
trigger_invalidation: If a retracement exceeds two-thirds of the prior trend, the move is technically a trend reversal and the prior trend is unlikely to resume. A pullback that turns into a countertrend move invalidates the continuation thesis.
risk_geometry: Entry at the MA on a pullback with stop below the pullback swing low (failure point); book recommends max stop distance 10% (swing) / 15% (investor); a trailing stop can ride the trend but expect to be stopped out one or more times during its evolution.
quote: When price moves too far away from that strong moving average, I refer to it as 'catching air.' ... When price has moved too far from the average, the stock may be overextended.

strategy_name: Reversal patterns require a directional move to reverse; stand aside in consolidation
mechanism: Reversal signals derive their meaning from reversing a prior move; in a sideways/consolidation regime there is no move to reverse, so patterns there are noise — and trend-following tools whipsaw in ranges.
setup_summary: Gate candlestick reversal families on regime: only fire after an identifiable directional move (up for bearish patterns, down for bullish ones), never inside a long consolidation/rectangle unless at the range extremes (where short swings give something to reverse). A sideways regime (flat/whipsawing 20-SMA, bounded peaks and bottoms) means standing aside for trend-following; false breakouts/breakdowns through range bounds are common. The book also weighs broad-market regime: broad sell-offs break even previously strong support.
trigger_invalidation: The book notes it is ambiguous at the right edge whether a range is consolidation or topping/bottoming base — the gate must not be rigid; the close-through of a range bound is the resolving event.
risk_geometry: Regime gate only; sets no entry/stop/target. It controls which behavior families are eligible (trend-following off in ranges).
quote: If price is moving sideways, referred to as consolidation, and a reversal pattern forms within that congestion area, it has little or no significance.

strategy_name: Signed order flow predicts short-term price change
setup_summary: Signed transaction volume (buys at ask minus sells at bid) accumulated over a look-back window predicts same-direction short-term price movement, because informed traders hit with market orders and market makers reprice. Falsifiable: regress next-interval return on trailing cumulative signed flow on BTCUSDT tape.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: cumulative/average signed order flow over the look-back is strongly positive (long) or negative (short). Invalidation: flow fails to predict (market makers already repriced), i.e., price does not follow flow direction within the horizon.
risk_geometry: Entry next interval open/close; stop = opposite flow reversal; target = R-multiple; expiry = short fixed horizon.

strategy_name: Post-event announcement drift: momentum from slow information diffusion
mechanism: price adjustments to new information complete gradually, so the market's own initial reaction direction persists into the session
setup_summary: After an earnings announcement made between prior close and today's open, buy at the open if the close-to-open return >= 0.5*std (90-day close-to-open std) and short if <= -0.5*std, liquidate at the same day's close. SPX universe: APR 6.7%, Sharpe 1.5 (Jan 2011-Apr 2012); overnight returns are on average negative. The trader does not interpret the news - the market's reaction is the signal. Duration of the drift has compressed from days (known since 1968) to intraday as awareness grew; other events (guidance, M&A, index composition changes) show the same pattern.
trigger_invalidation: Drift shortens below the bar horizon; announcement elicits no surprise (small reaction); macro news (FOMC, CPI) shows no significant drift in EURUSD.
risk_geometry: Entry at session open, exit at same-session close; intraday, no overnight carry; ~30 positions max daily.

strategy_name: Forced asset sales/purchases and constant-leverage rebalancing generate momentum
mechanism: mechanical flows (redemptions, inflows, constant-leverage rebalancing) buy and sell regardless of price, pushing prices in the flow direction and creating serial momentum that later reverts
setup_summary: Mutual funds facing >5% redemptions sell existing holdings, depressing prices and contagiously hurting other funds holding the same names; inflows cause the mirror (Coval-Stafford PRESSURE factor; market-neutral decile portfolio about 17% annualized, front-running predicted flows another 17%, post-pressure reversion 7%). Leveraged ETFs rebalancing to constant leverage near the close force buying after up days and selling after down days: buy DRN if the return to 15 minutes before close exceeds 2%, sell if below -2%, exit at close - APR 15%, Sharpe 1.8; a 1% SPX move needs ~17% of market-on-close volume traded by these funds. Crypto analog: liquidation cascades and funding-driven forced flows.
trigger_invalidation: Flow factor neutralized by offsetting investor flows; regime where flow-driven momentum reverses (August 2007 quant meltdown).
risk_geometry: PRESSURE factor: quarterly rebalance; leveraged-ETF trade: intraday entry/exit at close; time-based exits.
quote: Stocks disproportionately held by poorly performing mutual funds facing redemptions therefore experience negative returns. Furthermore, this asset 'fire sale'... is contagious.

strategy_name: Momentum crashes and regime alternation between momentum and mean reversion
mechanism: after a crisis, the rebound of crowded short positions and forced flows replaces momentum with strong mean reversion for years
setup_summary: Time-series and cross-sectional momentum strategies perform miserably for years after financial crises (Daniel-Moskowitz): the S&P DTI index was down -25.9% since Dec 2008; cross-sectional stock momentum was APR -30% in 2008-2009; after 1929 a representative momentum strategy took over 30 years to regain its high-water mark. Mean reversion is replaced by / replaces momentum regime-wise. Momentum thrives on kurtosis/black-swan events and is easy to risk-manage (limited downside); mean reversion has capped upside and can gap to catastrophic loss at max leverage.
trigger_invalidation: None ex-ante - this is a regime gate, not a tradable trigger; cannot be known in advance.

strategy_name: Stop-losses are structurally inconsistent with mean-reversion entries; time-based exits fit momentum
mechanism: a stop below a mean-reversion entry sits exactly where the reversion thesis strengthens, so stops contradict the entry logic; momentum entries have natural stop semantics (signal reversal)
setup_summary: Momentum strategies support both time-based and stop-loss exits (a reversed signal acts as a natural stop); downside is bounded, upside unlimited. Mean-reversion strategies cannot use stops without contradicting their entry signal - their upside is capped at the mean while downside is unbounded, so risk must be managed via position sizing, leverage, and the natural profit cap, not stops. Stop losses are also useless in markets that close (gap risk); 24/7 markets avoid the gap problem but not the logic contradiction.
trigger_invalidation: N/A - design rule.
risk_geometry: For mean-reversion experts: no ATR stop; use expiry/time-out and dead-thesis exit plus sized exposure. For momentum experts: stop and time exits both valid.

strategy_name: Donchian channel breakout with MACD momentum filter
mechanism: price taking out the X-day channel extreme resumes the prior trend; smoothed-momentum and MACD filters screen out counter-trend/false breakouts
setup_summary: Within a universe of markets ranked strongest/weakest by smoothed rate of change, buy a breakout above the X-day high (classic 20-day) when MACD is above zero and rising; short mirror on the Y-day low (10-day) when MACD below zero and falling. Pass the trade if the dollar risk from the X-day high to the Y-day low exceeds ~1% of core equity. Hard stop = Y-day low (longs).
trigger_invalidation: Hard stop (Y-day low) touched = small loss, exit and take the next signal; MACD flipping against direction cancels pending breakout consideration and invalidates the higher-TF thesis.
risk_geometry: Entry: stop/close through X-day high (longs) or Y-day low (shorts); initial hard stop = Y-day low (long) / X-day high (short), set immediately at fill and not moved; once trade works, replace hard stop with 39-period ATR trailing stop; no profit target; no expiry beyond stops.

strategy_name: Higher-timeframe trend retracement with 2-bar pullback stop entry
mechanism: the higher timeframe defines the tradable trend; a lower-timeframe retracement against it is transient, creating a low-risk continuation entry once price resumes the higher-TF direction
setup_summary: Weekly MACD positive and above zero (long setup) while the daily Elder Force / retracement oscillator crosses below zero (pullback); place a buy stop 1 tick (0.001%) above the high of the prior two bars and ratchet it lower each bar until filled or the weekly MACD reverses. Mirror for shorts. Hard stop = 1 tick below the two-bar low.
trigger_invalidation: If not filled, re-place the stop at each new bar; cancel the stop when the higher-timeframe MACD reverses. Hard stop hit = exit; thesis invalid only when higher-TF trend (weekly MACD) flips.
risk_geometry: Entry: buy stop 1 tick above prior 2-bar high (long) / sell stop below prior 2-bar low (short); hard stop = 2-bar low (long); replace with trailing ATR stop once in open profit (hold hard stop until ATR stop is tighter); position size = (1% of core equity) / (entry minus 2-bar low).

mechanism: relative strength persists: the strongest markets are most likely to keep trending higher and the weakest to keep falling, so the universe filter precedes the signal
setup_summary: Rank every candidate market by the average of three rate-of-change periods (e.g., 2/5/7) computed on the higher timeframe (weekly), smoothed to remove spikes; take long candidates only from the strongest decile and short candidates only from the weakest, then apply the 1%-risk gate before entry.
trigger_invalidation: A market falling out of the strong/weak ranking drops out of the candidate universe for new signals; open trades governed by stops, not by ranking.

strategy_name: Fixed-fractional 1% risk sizing on core equity
mechanism: risking a constant small fraction of true closed equity per trade keeps any single loss survivable across the long runs of losers trend following produces
setup_summary: Risk 0.75-1.25% of core equity (cash + closed positions, explicitly EXCLUDING open-trade profits) per trade. Position size = (cap% x core equity) / (entry minus hard-stop distance). Skip any trade whose computed risk exceeds the cap regardless of conviction.
trigger_invalidation: N/A — a sizing/admission rule; the trade is skipped when risk % exceeds the cap.
risk_geometry: Stop-based sizing: shares/contracts = (cap x core equity) / (entry - hard stop); core equity excludes open equity so a run-up cannot inflate position size.

Take trades ONLY in the direction of that major trend. On the lower timeframe (e.g., 30m/1h), buy pullbacks down to edge-defined support in an uptrend; sell rallies up to edge-defined resistance in a downtrend. All entry and exit signals are computed on the same (lower) timeframe; the longer timeframe is a filter only.

strategy_name: Bollinger-band squeeze breakout with band expansion
mechanism: Tight consolidation compresses volatility; a close through the band with band expansion signals a momentum continuation in the direction of the breach
setup_summary: After a multi-week range with tight recent consolidation (narrow Bollinger bandwidth / low ATR percentile), enter LONG on a bar close above the upper band accompanied by band widening, SHORT on a close below the lower band; 'the steeper the expansion of the band, the stronger the trend.' Book's USD/CAD example: 5 weeks range-bound, tight consolidation, pierce of upper Bollinger = breakout trigger; a volume surge on the break confirms (breakouts 'accompanied by a widening of the band... underscoring the momentum').
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: close outside band after compression + band expansion + volume surge. Invalidation: close returns inside the band (false breakout) or band fails to expand; book notes the breakout often begins before bands react (lagging).
risk_geometry: Entry: next-bar-close after band breach; stop: band midline or recent swing extreme (book example used a hard stop above prior resistance to cap loss at 50 PIPs); target: extension or ride until CCI/MACD cross zero-line (partial exit); expiry ~1 week in book example.
quote: Bollinger bands, then, are especially useful for forecasting breakouts. In general, the steeper the expansion of the band, the stronger the trend.
chapter_anchor: Ch.6 'Moving Average Envelopes and Bollinger Bands' pp.151-154; Ch.7 pp.172-173
notes: 24/7 market with no gaps removes the overnight-gap failure mode of squeeze breakouts; high leverage rewards the low-risk entry. Distinct from the backlogged breakout_retest (which requires location/prior-high refs); this family keys on volatility compression + band expansion.

strategy_name: Mechanical MA-cross trend system with momentum confirmation (5x5)
mechanism: Trend initiation is signaled by short MA crossing long MA; confirmation from an oscillator on the same side of its midline; trade until the opposite signal
setup_summary: Fully rule-based and backtestable: 'a so-called 5 x 5 system will generate a buy signal when the close price is above a specified simple moving average (SMA) and the Relative Strength Index (RSI) is above the mid-line 50. A sell signal will be generated when the close price is below the SMA and the RSI is below the mid-line 50.' Book also documents a 5-day/20-day MA cross + MACD variant that held a 1,000-PIP short for 2 months on EUR/USD.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: close-side of SMA + RSI-side agreement (or MA cross). Invalidation: whipsaw back across the cross (book shows the rule produced two false signals and missed a 1,000-PIP counter-move); entry after the move has already happened (MA is a following indicator).
risk_geometry: Entry: next bar after confirmed cross; exit: opposite cross (system held until reversal signal, no fixed expiry); stop: MA on the opposite side or ATR multiple; target: none (ride until opposite signal) - book warns simple MA rules' edge decayed by early 1990s in liquid majors.
quote: When the 5-day moving average crosses the 20-day average, it heralds a trend reversal... I will enter a position upon the next trend reversal and close it out after the following trend reversal.
chapter_anchor: Ch.6 'Moving Averages' pp.148-151; Ch.7 'Purely Technical Strategy' pp.169-174
notes: Directly expressible as a V8 Expert consuming ema/sma features. strategy_name: Extreme positioning contrarian (squeeze fuel)
mechanism: When speculative positioning reaches an extreme against the prevailing price trend, the market is squeezed upon any reversal, amplifying the move
setup_summary: When a positioning proxy reaches an extreme (book: COT short positions at extreme as EUR/USD bottomed June 2010), buy the reversal on trend-confirmation (MA cross), expecting a short squeeze 'potentially catapulting the euro upward by hundreds of PIPs in only a few days.' Related OI signal: NZD's sustained 2011 rise was preceded by OI bottoming.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: extreme positioning (e.g., >2 std dev from its distribution) + price begins reversing. Invalidation: positioning keeps extending with the trend (no reversal); COT/OI is a lagging snapshot, so entry must be confirmed by price action.
risk_geometry: Entry: next-bar close after reversal confirmation (book used MA crossover as confirmation); stop: beyond the extreme level; target: squeeze extension measured in hundreds of PIPs over days; expiry: a few days to weeks.
quote: the Commitments of Traders data showed that short positions had reached an extreme level. This development alone would be reason enough to buy the euro, since once an uptrend started, it would cause a short squeeze.

strategy_name: Scheduled-news overshoot and pre-release breakout straddle
mechanism: Markets overshoot around scheduled data: expectations are pre-positioned before the release, the print triggers a sharp move, then reaction reverses if the data disappointed relative to consensus
setup_summary: Around a high-impact scheduled release, price consolidates in the hours before; place OCO buy-stop above and sell-stop below the consolidation channel so the breakout direction triggers automatically ('One-Cancels-Other... if the breakout is to the upside, then the buy order will be triggered and the sell order will be cancelled'). Separately, 'buy the rumor, sell the news': fade the extension once the print is in line with (or beats) expectations - a 100-PIP USD rally on a beat reversed within the same day. The book's EUR/USD employment-data example had a 50-PIP pre-release buildup.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: scheduled event + tight consolidation channel. Invalidation: false breakout when bands are set too close (book's own example was stopped by one); a data print exactly matching consensus produces no overshoot.
risk_geometry: Entry: OCO stop orders at channel boundaries (or market on release); stop: opposite channel side or beyond the channel; target: 50-100 PIPs in book examples; expiry: same session - event volatility decays within hours.
quote: With both types of news, the market has a propensity to overshoot, hence the expression, 'Buy the rumor, sell the news.'

strategy_name: Parabolic SAR stop-and-reverse (documented negative result)
mechanism: The claimed mechanism is that trends need rapid momentum accumulation; the Parabolic SAR predicts trend starts/ends via dots, but the book's own worked chart shows it was wrong more often than right
setup_summary: Rejected method: a stop-and-reverse dot signal used to time trend entry/exit. The book applies it to EUR/USD and reports 'the Parabolic SAR was ultimately more often wrong than it was right!', even advising a 3-dot (3-period) delay to build in margin of error. risk_geometry: None adopted; the book's example shows both entries and stops whipsawed.

strategy_name: Turtle System 2 — 55-day Donchian channel breakout
setup_summary: On daily bars, when price trades a single tick above the highest high of the prior 55 sessions, buy 1 unit; when it trades a tick below the lowest low of the prior 55 sessions, sell 1 unit. Entry is executed intraday at the breakout tick (not at the close); if the market gaps through the breakout level, enter at the open. All 55-day breakouts are taken regardless of the prior breakout's result.
trigger_invalidation: Valid while price continues through the channel extreme; thesis invalidated when the System 2 exit (20-day low for longs / 20-day high for shorts) trades through.
risk_geometry: Entry: intraday touch (limit) or gap-open. Stop: 2N (2% equity risk). Target: none fixed — held via trailing 20-day channel exit. No expiry.
quote: We entered when the price exceeded by a single tick the high or low of the preceding 55 days. All breakouts for System 2 would be taken whether or not the previous breakout had been a winner.
chapter_anchor: Bonus Chapter 'Original Turtle Trading Rules', 'System 2 Entry', pp. 260-261
notes: Canonical, falsifiable trend-following entry; 24/7 perp market removes futures gap/open complexities and contract rolls, making the channel breakout directly executable on BTCUSDT. Entry-at-touch semantics conflict with V8's canonical fill-at-close simulator, so it needs an explicit fill rule (touch-fill or next-bar-open). Budget-gated: add as backlog family, challenger to trend_pullback via registry experiment on frozen OOS.

strategy_name: Turtle System 1 — 20-day breakout with post-winner skip + 55-day failsafe
setup_summary: 20-day channel breakout entry, but the signal is skipped if the last breakout in that same market was a winner (a breakout counts as a loser if price moved 2N against the position before a profitable 10-day exit; direction of the prior breakout is irrelevant). If a System 1 signal is skipped because the prior trade won, the entry point becomes the 55-day breakout as a failsafe so major moves are not missed.
trigger_invalidation: Entry is suppressed only when the prior breakout in that market was a winner; the 55-day failsafe level always remains as a valid backstop entry.
risk_geometry: Entry: intraday tick / gap-open. Stop: 2N. Exit: System 1 10-day low/high (all units). No fixed target.
quote: System 1 breakout entry signals would be ignored if the last breakout would have resulted in a winning trade... this 55-day breakout was considered the failsafe breakout point.
chapter_anchor: Bonus Chapter 'Original Turtle Trading Rules', 'System 1 Entry', pp. 259-260
notes: Mechanism: filtering breakouts that follow a recent winner avoids the whipsaw of repeated breakout attempts, while the failsafe preserves trend capture. Concrete testable variant of donchian_breakout (structural entry-filter difference, not a threshold change, so a distinct family). 'Last breakout outcome' is also a candidate history-group feature. Directly implementable on BTC 1h/daily with continuous data.

strategy_name: Turtle unit pyramiding — add 1 unit per 1/2N favorable move
setup_summary: After the initial 1-unit breakout entry, add 1 unit each time price moves 1/2N favorably from the prior fill price, up to the 4-unit per-market maximum; the add interval is measured from the actual fill, so slippage extends the next add distance. If the market moves fast enough, all 4 units can be added in a single day.
trigger_invalidation: Adds stop at the max-unit cap for that market; each add raises all prior stops by 1/2N (see atr_stop finding).
risk_geometry: Add interval: 1/2N from prior fill; whole-position stop trails 2N from the newest unit.
quote: Turtles entered single-unit long positions at the breakouts and added to those positions at 1/2N intervals after their initial entry.
chapter_anchor: Bonus Chapter 'Original Turtle Trading Rules', 'Adding Units', pp. 260-261
notes: Scaling speed is load-bearing: the book warns that adding units slowly (a 'conservative' delay) increases the chance a retracement hits the stops, inverting profitability — a falsifiable claim about build-out cadence inside an episode. Compatible with V8's one-exposure-per-direction rule (units scale within a single exposure). Perp fractional sizing makes 1/2N increments trivially executable; funding cost scales with the added exposure.

strategy_name: Turtle channel exits: full position on 10-day (System 1) / 20-day (System 2) counter-breakout
setup_summary: Exit the entire position when price makes a new N-day low (long) or high (short): 10-day for System 1, 20-day for System 2. Stops are not pre-placed with the broker; the trader watches and exits via limit/market order once the exit price trades through. Most breakout trades lose; profitability depends on a few large winners being held through 20-100% profit give-back.
trigger_invalidation: Exit fires on the counter-channel breakout; theses-invalid and re-entry only on a fresh breakout.
risk_geometry: No fixed target; exit trails at the N-day channel, requiring tolerance for giving back large unrealized profits.
quote: The System 1 exit was a 10-day low for long positions and a 10-day high for short positions... The System 2 exit was a 20-day low for long positions and a 20-day high for short positions. All the units in the position would be exited if the price went against the position for a 20-day breakout.

strategy_name: EMA crossover trading system (backtested)
setup_summary: On a daily (or per-book 1h-analog) chart, when the fast EMA crosses above the slow EMA, initiate a long; when it crosses below, initiate a short; the book backtests this exact rule on EUR/CHF daily over 6 months and finds it net profitable but with negative Sharpe and risk-to-reward ratios, i.e. profit earned at excessive return variability.
trigger_invalidation: The reverse EMA cross exits the position; the book's own backtest flags negative risk-adjusted return as the invalidation of the naive cross as-is.
risk_geometry: Entry at bar close on cross; no stop/target stated in the book (position held through opposite cross); book evaluates with risk-to-reward and Sharpe/Sortino.
quote: each time the EMA crossed over the moving average, the computer initiated a hypothetical buy or sell order.

strategy_name: One-Cancels-Other breakout bracket (direction-uncertain breakout)
setup_summary: When you expect a breakout but not the direction, place a One-Cancels-Other bracket: a buy stop 30 PIPs above the current rate and a sell stop 30 PIPs below; whichever trigger fills first, the other cancels automatically (example: EUR/USD buy +30 or sell -30, whichever happens first).
trigger_invalidation: Neither trigger fills before the order's expiry (one hour, one day, or GTC); after a fill, the thesis dies if price immediately returns through the reference range (failed breakout).
risk_geometry: Entry: stop-limit at +/-30 PIPs from current price; order expiry is set by the trader; protective stop on the triggered position placed by the trader (not specified by the book).
quote: you could indicate a One-Cancels-Other order that either executes a buy if the EUR/USD rate increases 30 PIPs or executes a sell if it falls 30 PIPs, whatever happens first.
chapter_anchor: Chapter 9, Order Entry
notes: Perps have native 24/7 stop-limit orders and no overnight gaps, so the OCO bracket is fully implementable on BTCUSDT 1h. In V8 this is a breakout behavior family over a windowed high/low reference range; V8 rule 16 (one exposure per direction) means the two bracket sides map to two separate candidate episodes rather than one dual-direction expert.

strategy_name: Turtle/Donchian channel breakout (System 1 & 2)
mechanism: A breakout of a prior N-day high/low signals a new trend; the edge comes from riding continuation after resistance/support is exceeded
setup_summary: On daily bars (for V8: BTCUSDT 1h): buy when the close exceeds the highest high of the prior N days (N=20 for System 1, N=60 for System 2); sell short on the mirroring low break. Entry sized so the initial stop (2N = 2 ATR) risks 2% of equity; positions pyramided in 1/2-N increments up to 4 units; exit via the 2N stop-loss and, per Chapter 10's Donchian Trend variant, a 10-day breakout exit plus a 25/350 EMA trend filter.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: close (or next open) beyond a windowed prior extreme. Invalidation: close falls back inside the channel / hits the 2N stop; the 17-consecutive-losing-cocoa-trades table (Table 4-1) shows long losing streaks are the normal cost of the entry.
risk_geometry: entry: next-bar open after breakout close (Turtles used limit orders); stop: 2N (2 ATR) below/above entry, equivalent to 2% of account at unit sizing; targets: none pre-set - let trend run, exit on 10/20-day breakout in opposite direction (bonus chapter, Part 2) or time; expiry: none (trend-following hold); pyramiding: up to 4 units in 1/2-N increments.
quote: The basic idea was to buy if a market exceeded the highest price for a particular number of preceding days, that is, broke out of its prior price levels.
chapter_anchor: Ch.3 The First $2 Million Is the Toughest (pp.38-40, 44-45); Ch.10 Turtle-Style Trading: Step by Step (pp.139-140)
notes: The canonical turtle system and the most likely-corroborated strategy in this library; directly testable on 24/7 BTC 1h (no overnight gaps to stop through). Note the book's own finding that Donchian's edge decayed post-Turtle era (Ch.10: CAGR 29.4%, worst of six systems in 1996-2006) - crowding. V8 budget: would compete for a trend-continuation slot with trend_pullback; propose as new family (registry PROPOSED), not a variant of breakout_retest.

strategy_name: Trend portfolio filter (fast MA vs slow MA direction gate)
mechanism: Filtering entries to the direction of the longer-term moving-average trend removes breakouts against the major trend, which are the moves least likely to continue; market-state selection is a separable source of edge from the entry itself
setup_summary: Compute a fast MA (50-day, or 25-day EMA in the Donchian Trend test version) and a slow MA (300-day, or 350-day EMA). Permit long entries only when fast > slow and short entries only when fast < slow. Book's quantified claim: random entries become edge-bearing under the filter (E70-ratio 1.27 vs ~1.0 unfiltered) and a 20-day breakout entry goes from E70 1.20 to 1.33 with the filter added, E120 reaching ~1.6.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: fast MA crosses to the favorable side of slow MA. Invalidation/filter: no new trades when the two MAs are on the 'wrong' side; the filter also acts as the regime switch for the four market states (trending-quiet vs trending-volatile vs stable states from Ch.2).
risk_geometry: Not a trade geometry - a portfolio/regime gate applied before entries; no stops or expiry of its own.
quote: you can initiate long trades only in markets in which the 50-day moving average is higher than the 300-day moving average and can initiate short trades only in markets in which the 50-day moving average is lower than the 300-day moving average.
chapter_anchor: Ch.5 Trading with an Edge, The Trend Portfolio Filter Edge (pp.69-73); Ch.2 market states (pp.25-27)
notes: Strongest quantitative claim in Part 1: the filter is where much of the trend edge lives (70,000-random-entry test, E70=1.27). Maps directly to a V8 regime filter gating existing trend families (trend_pullback, donchian breakout) - fast/slow MA direction on 1h BTC is trivially computable and PIT-safe. The Ch.2 four-market-state taxonomy (stable-quiet / stable-volatile / trending-quiet / trending-volatile) is the underlying regime framework and belongs in the same register decision.

strategy_name: Volatility channel breakout (ATR Channel and Bollinger Breakout)
mechanism: A move beyond a channel defined by a long moving average plus a volatility buffer (ATR or standard deviation) signals volatility expansion and the start of a trend; the wide buffer filters false moves in quiet markets
setup_summary: ATR Channel Breakout: channel top = 350-day MA of close + 7 ATR, bottom = 350-day MA - 3 ATR; enter long at the open if the prior close exceeded the top, short if below the bottom; exit when close crosses back through the 350-day MA. Bollinger Breakout variant: 350-day MA +/- 2.5 std dev of close. Backtests (Table 10-1, 1996-2006): ATR CBO CAGR 49.5%/MAR 1.24; Bollinger CBO CAGR 51.8%/MAR 1.52 - both beat Donchian Trend.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: prior-bar close beyond the volatility channel. Invalidation: close returns inside the channel (exit at MA) - no stop used in the book's base version; unit limits still apply.
risk_geometry: entry: next-bar open after close beyond channel; stop: none in base version (exit = close crossing back through the 350-day MA); target: none (trend); expiry: none.
quote: The channel is formed by adding 7 ATR to a 350-day moving average of the closing prices for the channel top and subtracting 3 ATR from the moving average for the channel bottom.
chapter_anchor: Ch.10 Turtle-Style Trading: Step by Step, ATR Channel Breakout & Bollinger Breakout (pp.136-139); Ch.9 building blocks (p.127)
notes: The ATR-channel is effectively the PGO system (Mark Johnson, Ch.10). On 24/7 crypto the long 350-bar MA on 1h needs ~2 weeks of warm-up data; the volatility-buffer width makes the filter robust to regime vol changes. Fits V8 feature groups volatility+trend; a natural new family distinct from donchian (channel vs raw window breakout).

strategy_name: Fixed-duration time exit (80 bars, no stop)
mechanism: A fixed holding-period exit lets a trade run exactly long enough to capture the trend while mechanically capping drawdown from trend reversal; the book's tests show time exits beat breakout exits and that adding stops makes trend systems strictly worse
setup_summary: Donchian Trend with Time Exit: same 20-day breakout entry with 25/350 EMA trend filter, but exit after exactly 80 days and no stop. It posted the best CAGR of all six tested systems (57.2%, MAR 1.31, Table 10-1) and was the only system whose metrics were unchanged when 5 adverse months were appended (Table 10-2/10-3). Companion finding (Adding Stops, pp.145-147): for Dual/Triple MA and Donchian Time, every stop width from ~0.5 to ~10 ATR made every metric (CAGR, MAR, Sharpe, drawdown) worse; only stops >= 10 ATR matched no-stop.
trigger_invalidation: Exit is calendar-based (N bars after entry) regardless of price; no thesis-based invalidation in the base system.
risk_geometry: entry: next-bar open on 20-day breakout; stop: none; target: none; expiry: fixed 80 bars - the risk_geometry expiry IS the strategy.
quote: uses a time-based exit instead of a breakout exit. It exits the trade after 80 days and does not use any stops whatsoever.

notes: Directly refines V8's expiry_bars risk geometry (trend_pullback already uses expiry_bars=8): this book supports long fixed time exits for trend-continuation families and cautions against entry-based ATR stops for slow systems. strategy_name: Turtle unit limits (4/market, 6 correlated, 10-12 per direction)
mechanism: Hard caps on aggregate exposure per market, per correlated basket, and per direction protect against the correlated, simultaneous adverse moves at trend breakdowns; the per-market cap also acts as a filter that keeps out late-signaling lagging markets
setup_summary: Max 4 units per market; max 6 units total across highly correlated markets (e.g., the four interest-rate products, the six currencies); max 10 units long or 10 short overall (12 if positions in uncorrelated markets). Correlated markets naturally cluster: in a real move, all four interest-rate products signal but the Turtles typically held only the first two - the cap filters out markets that signal last and move least.
trigger_invalidation: N/A - a risk gate, not a signal; violations block new units until exposure unwinds.
risk_geometry: Aggregate exposure cap in unit terms (unit = 1% equity risk); the author credits these caps with saving Richard Dennis well over $100M on the Oct 1987 single-day shock.
quote: we could put on a maximum of only 4 units per market; second, we could put on a maximum of only 6 units in markets that were highly correlated; third, we could put on a maximum of only 10 units in any given direction (i.e., 10 long or 10 short).

notes: The 'everything moves against you at once' claim (pp.119, 201-202) is even stronger in crypto, where BTC/ETH/alt perps share funding regimes and liquidation cascades. The lagging-market filter property is a genuine selection mechanism for correlated alt baskets.

strategy_name: Countertrend fade at support/resistance anchors
mechanism: Anchoring + recency + disposition make recent swing highs/lows sticky anchors: traders sell into rallies to prior highs and buy into prior lows, producing bounces; the short-term edge of betting against a fresh breakout is real because most new-high breakouts fail
setup_summary: Near a recent swing high (resistance anchor), sell short expecting a bounce/fade; near a recent swing low (support anchor), buy expecting a bounce; stop beyond the anchor level. Supporting evidence: the E-ratio for 20-day breakouts is below 1.0 over the first few days after the signal, i.e., price on average moves against a breakout in the very short term, then flips positive only at medium horizons (Figure 5-2).
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: price approaches a windowed prior extreme with no close beyond it. Invalidation: close breaks the anchor level - the book's heating-oil example (Sept 5, 2006) shows fading a broken support leads to a full wipeout; countertrend traders must exit on the close at or just after the breakdown.
risk_geometry: entry: bar close at/near anchor; stop: ~0.05-0.06 beyond the S/R level (book's example: buy at $2.10, stop 6c below at support breakdown); target: toward the opposite anchor (structure), not an R-multiple; expiry: short (very short-term edge only).
quote: there is generally more movement against a trade taken at a breakout than there is in the direction of the breakout. This is one of the reasons you can make money using a countertrend trading style by betting on the breakout not holding and in favor of a bounce off of the support or resistance.
chapter_anchor: Ch.5 Trading with an Edge (pp.68-69); Ch.6 Falling Off the Edge (pp.75-84)
notes: The short-term adverse-breakout data is empirical (E-ratio < 1.0 early), but no full countertrend system is backtested in Part 1 - mechanism rests on the cognitive-bias narrative. Perp caveats: funding keeps price pinned near anchors, liquidation cascades make breakdowns sharper than futures (higher tail risk on the fade), and round-number/ liquidation-level anchors in crypto differ from exchange-made swing anchors. Candidate backlog family (mean_reversion class) alongside V8's existing trend and liquidity families.
